title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: What is an ICT Weekly Profile?
content:
#### What is an ICT Weekly Profile?

An ICT Weekly Profile is a conceptual framework that describes a typical pattern of price behaviour during a trading week. Each profile has unique characteristics — a specific day on which the weekly high or low forms, a specific direction of the dominant move, and a specific higher-timeframe condition that makes that profile likely.

These profiles are not fixed predictions. They are weekly tendencies that institutions tend to deliver, and the trader who recognises which profile is in play has a meaningful edge in positioning early in the week.

The 12 profiles below cover the dominant patterns. In any given week, price will follow one of them. Reading the higher-timeframe premium / discount context on Monday tells me which one is most likely.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: (I) Classic Tuesday Low of the Week
content:
#### (I) Classic Tuesday Low of the Week

**Bullish Profile:** When price is in a bullish higher-timeframe context, it may manipulate on Monday and hover above a higher-timeframe discount array. Then on Tuesday it drops into the higher-timeframe discount array to form the low of the week.

![Classic Tuesday Low of the Week — bullish profile chart showing Monday hover above discount array, Tuesday drop into discount, weekly low](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/classic-tuesday-low.png)

To anticipate this profile, you should know the higher-timeframe discount array. When the market fails to drop into the discount array on Monday, it is most likely that Tuesday will see the drive lower to mark the weekly low in London or New York session.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: (II) Classic Tuesday High of the Week
content:
#### (II) Classic Tuesday High of the Week

**Bearish Profile:** When price is in a bearish higher-timeframe context, it may manipulate on Monday and hover below a higher-timeframe premium array. Then on Tuesday it rises into the higher-timeframe premium array to form the high of the week.

![Classic Tuesday High of the Week — bearish profile chart showing Monday hover below premium array, Tuesday rise into premium, weekly high](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/classic-tuesday-high.png)

To anticipate this, you should know the higher-timeframe [Premium](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-premium-and-discount-zone-identification/> "Premium") array. When the market fails to rise into the premium array on Monday, it is most likely that Tuesday will see the drive higher to mark the weekly high in London or New York session.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: (III) Wednesday Low of the Week
content:
#### (III) Wednesday Low of the Week

**Bullish Profile:** When price is bullish, it may manipulate on Monday and Tuesday and hover above a higher-timeframe discount array. Then on Wednesday it drops into the higher-timeframe discount array to form the low of the week.

![Wednesday Low of the Week — bullish profile chart with two-day Monday-Tuesday consolidation before Wednesday drop into discount array](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/wednesday-low-of-week.png)

To anticipate this, you should know the higher-timeframe [Discount](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-premium-and-discount-zone-identification/> "Discount") [Array](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-pd-array-key-to-trade-execution/> "Array"). When the market fails to drop into the discount array on Monday and Tuesday, it is most likely that Wednesday will see the drive lower to mark the weekly low in London or New York session.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: (IV) Wednesday High of the Week
content:
#### (IV) Wednesday High of the Week

**Bearish Profile:** When price is bearish, it may manipulate on Monday and Tuesday and hover below a higher-timeframe premium array. Then on Wednesday it rises into the higher-timeframe premium array to form the high of the week.

![Wednesday High of the Week — bearish profile chart with two-day Monday-Tuesday consolidation before Wednesday rise into premium array](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/wednesday-high-of-week.png)

To anticipate this, you should know the higher-timeframe premium array. When the market fails to rise into the premium array on Monday and Tuesday, it is most likely that Wednesday will see the drive higher to mark the weekly high in London or New York session.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: (V) Consolidation Thursday Bullish Reversal
content:
#### (V) Consolidation Thursday Bullish Reversal

When price is bullish, it may consolidate Monday through Wednesday, then runs the intra-week low and rejects it forming a market reversal.

![Consolidation Thursday Bullish Reversal — three-day consolidation, Thursday liquidity raid below intra-week low, sharp bullish reversal](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/thursday-bullish-reversal.png)

To anticipate this, you must know the higher-timeframe discount array. When price fails to drop into the higher-timeframe discount array, it is likely that Thursday will see a drive lower on market-driver news or an interest rate release in late New York session, around 02:00 PM New York local time.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: (VI) Consolidation Thursday Bearish Reversal
content:
#### (VI) Consolidation Thursday Bearish Reversal

When price is bearish, it may consolidate Monday through Wednesday, then runs the intra-week high and rejects it forming a market reversal.

![Consolidation Thursday Bearish Reversal — three-day consolidation, Thursday liquidity raid above intra-week high, sharp bearish reversal](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/thursday-reversal.png)

To anticipate this, you must know the higher-timeframe premium array. When price fails to rise into the higher-timeframe premium array, it is likely that Thursday will see a drive higher on market-driver news or an interest rate release in late New York session, around 02:00 PM New York local time.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: (VII) Consolidation Midweek Rally
content:
#### (VII) Consolidation Midweek Rally

**Bullish Profile:** When price is bullish and consolidates Monday through Wednesday, then runs into the intra-week high and expands higher into Friday.

![Consolidation Midweek Rally — three-day consolidation followed by bullish expansion through intra-week high into Friday](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/midweek-rally.png)

**How to anticipate.** When price is bullish and has yet to run to the premium array on the higher timeframe, and it has recently rallied from a discount array and simply paused without any bearish reversal price action — that indicates price is about to expand higher for the premium array.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: (VIII) Consolidation Midweek Decline
content:
#### (VIII) Consolidation Midweek Decline

**Bearish Profile:** When price is bearish and consolidates Monday through Wednesday, then runs into the intra-week low and expands lower into Friday.

![Consolidation Midweek Decline — three-day consolidation followed by bearish expansion through intra-week low into Friday](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/midweek-decline.png)

**How to anticipate.** When price is bearish and has yet to run to the discount array on the higher timeframe, and it has recently declined from a premium array and simply paused without any bullish reversal price action — that indicates price is about to expand lower for the discount array.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: (IX) Seek and Destroy Bullish Friday
content:
#### (IX) Seek and Destroy Bullish Friday

**Neutral-Low Probability Profile:** When price consolidates Monday through Thursday running shallow stops under and above the intra-week high, then runs the intra-week high and expands higher into Friday.

![Seek and Destroy Bullish Friday — choppy four-day consolidation followed by Friday upside expansion through intra-week high](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/destroy-bullish-friday.png)

**How to anticipate.** When the market is awaiting interest rate announcements or Non-Farm Payroll, it can create this profile in the summer months of July and August. Better to avoid trading in these conditions.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: (X) Seek and Destroy Bearish Friday
content:
#### (X) Seek and Destroy Bearish Friday

**Neutral-Low Probability Profile:** When price consolidates Monday through Thursday running shallow stops under and above the intra-week high, then runs the intra-week low and expands lower into Friday.

![Seek and Destroy Bearish Friday — choppy four-day consolidation followed by Friday downside expansion through intra-week low](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/destroy-bearish-friday.png)

**How to anticipate.** When the market is awaiting interest rate announcements or Non-Farm Payroll, it can create this profile in the summer months of July and August. Better to avoid trading in these conditions. For the dedicated breakdown of this Friday-specific reversal pattern, see the [ICT Seek and Destroy Friday](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-seek-and-destroy-friday/>) guide.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: (XI) Wednesday Weekly Bullish Reversal
content:
#### (XI) Wednesday Weekly Bullish Reversal

When price is bullish and consolidates Monday through Tuesday, then drives lower into the higher-timeframe discount array on Wednesday to induce sell stops, and then strongly reverses.

![Wednesday Weekly Bullish Reversal — Monday-Tuesday consolidation, Wednesday drive into discount array, sell-stop liquidity raid, strong reversal](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/weekly-bullish-reversal.png)

When the market is trading at the long-term or intermediate-term low, price will pair institutional buying with pending sell-side liquidity — the classic sell-stops raid before the reversal.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: (XII) Wednesday Weekly Bearish Reversal
content:
#### (XII) Wednesday Weekly Bearish Reversal

When price is bearish and consolidates Monday through Tuesday, then drives higher into the higher-timeframe premium array on Wednesday to induce buy stops, and then strongly reverses.

![Wednesday Weekly Bearish Reversal — Monday-Tuesday consolidation, Wednesday drive into premium array, buy-stop liquidity raid, strong reversal](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/weekly-bearish-reversal.png)

When the market is trading at the long-term or intermediate-term high, price will pair institutional selling with pending buy-side liquidity — the classic buy-stops raid before the reversal.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: How to Use ICT Weekly Profiles in Your Trading
content:
#### How to Use ICT Weekly Profiles in Your Trading

The Weekly Profiles are not a setup in themselves — they are a directional framework that tells me what to expect for the week. I use them as the weekly anchor on top of which I run intraday models like the Silver Bullet, the OTE, and the 1st Presented FVG.

The workflow I run every Monday morning:

  1. **Read the higher-timeframe context** on the daily and weekly charts. Is price bullish or bearish on the higher timeframe? Is there a clear premium or discount array still untouched?
  2. **Identify the most likely profile** based on the daily-bias and PD-array conditions. If the higher-timeframe discount sits below current price and the bias is bullish, expect a Tuesday Low or Wednesday Low profile. If price has consolidated for two days without reaching the array, the bias-aligned profile becomes more probable.
  3. **Set the weekly target** — the high or low you expect to print, and the day you expect it to print on. This is the directional anchor for every intraday trade in that week.
  4. **Run intraday setups in the direction of the profile.** If the Tuesday Low profile is in play, every Monday and early-Tuesday intraday entry should align toward shorting into the discount array, then reversing for the bullish move once the weekly low forms.
  5. **Adjust mid-week if the profile invalidates.** If by Wednesday close the expected weekly extreme has not formed, price has likely shifted to a different profile. Re-read the chart from the new conditions.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: USA Trading Note — ES & NQ Futures
content:
#### USA Trading Note — ES & NQ Futures

For US-based traders, the Weekly Profiles are most reliable on US index futures — **NASDAQ 100 (NQ Futures)** and the **E-mini S &P 500 (ES Futures)**. The CME futures session structure makes the day-by-day profile read very clean. ES and NQ are CFTC-regulated futures and execute through a US futures broker (NinjaTrader, AMP, Tradovate, or a prop firm such as Topstep). The major USD forex pairs (GBP/USD, EUR/USD) and Gold (XAU/USD) also respect Weekly Profile mechanics. TradingView is for chart analysis only.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: Common Mistakes I See Traders Make on Weekly Profiles
content:
#### Common Mistakes I See Traders Make on Weekly Profiles

Five mistakes account for the majority of failed Weekly Profile reads. Avoid these and the framework converts at a much higher rate.

  1. **Reading the profile without the higher-timeframe PD Array context.** The profiles are anchored to the higher-timeframe premium and discount arrays. Without identifying those levels first, you cannot tell which profile is in play. Always set the PD Array context before assigning the profile.
  2. **Forcing a profile early in the week.** By Monday close, only a few profiles can be ruled out — most are still possible. Wait for Tuesday and Wednesday’s price action to narrow the read. Do not commit to a profile prematurely.
  3. **Trading the Friday Seek-and-Destroy profiles.** Profile IX and X are explicitly low-probability and tied to NFP / interest-rate uncertainty. The right play is to skip those weeks, not trade them harder.
  4. **Ignoring 02:00 PM NY local on Thursdays.** Profiles V and VI both pivot around the late-NY news drive. If you are not aware of the day’s news calendar, you will misread the move as random when it is actually the profile delivering on schedule.
  5. **Treating the profile as a guarantee.** The profiles are tendencies, not predictions. Any given week can fail to follow any profile. Always run risk management as if the profile read could be wrong.

title: ict-weekly-range-profiles
section: FAQs About ICT Weekly Profiles
content:
#### FAQs About ICT Weekly Profiles

**What are ICT Weekly Profiles?**

ICT Weekly Profiles are 12 conceptual frameworks Michael Huddleston taught for reading the typical day-by-day delivery of price across a trading week. Each profile describes a different pattern for how the high and low of the week are likely to form.

**How many ICT Weekly Profiles are there?**

Twelve. They cover the Tuesday Low and High patterns, the Wednesday Low and High patterns, four Consolidation profiles (Thursday Reversals and Midweek Expansions), the two low-probability Friday Seek-and-Destroy profiles, and two Wednesday Weekly Reversal profiles.

**Which Weekly Profile prints most often?**

The Tuesday Low (in bullish weeks) and Tuesday High (in bearish weeks) are the most common in normal market conditions. The Consolidation Thursday Reversals are the next most frequent, especially during weeks with major news releases.

**How do I anticipate which Weekly Profile is in play?**

Read the higher-timeframe premium / discount arrays. The profile that is most likely is the one whose end state — Tuesday low into discount, Wednesday high into premium, Thursday reversal at intra-week extreme — aligns with the higher-timeframe bias and untouched arrays.

**What is the Seek and Destroy Friday profile?**

It is a low-probability profile where price chops Monday through Thursday running shallow stops on both sides, then expands sharply on Friday. It tends to print around major news events like NFP and rate decisions, especially in the summer months. Avoid trading these weeks.

**What is the difference between Wednesday High of the Week and Wednesday Weekly Bearish Reversal?**

The Wednesday High (profile IV) is the bearish weekly delivery — Wednesday is just where the weekly high prints. The Wednesday Weekly Bearish Reversal (profile XII) is the opposite — price drives into Wednesday’s high to raid buy stops at a long-term high, then reverses sharply for the rest of the week. Different intent, different trade direction.

**Can Weekly Profiles be used on forex?**

Yes. The profiles are most reliable on US index futures (NQ, ES) but the major forex pairs (GBP/USD, EUR/USD) and Gold (XAU/USD) also respect the same weekly delivery patterns.

**What timeframe do I use to read the Weekly Profiles?**

Daily for the day-by-day pattern, weekly for the higher-timeframe PD Array context, and 4-hour for the intra-day timing of weekly highs and lows. For intraday execution within a profile, drop to the 15-minute and 5-minute as usual.

**Should I trade the Weekly Profile or skip the week?**

Trade weeks where the higher-timeframe context clearly supports one of the high-probability profiles (I through VIII, XI, XII). Skip weeks that fit profile IX or X (Seek and Destroy Friday) — the choppy stop-hunt action makes execution unreliable.

# Inducement After Break of Structure (BOS) — Minor BOS & New Inducement Identification

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/inducement-after-break-of-structure/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/inducement-after-break-of-structure/)

![Inducement after break of structure \(BOS\) — minor BOS confirms a new inducement level when the original inducement was not swept](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Inducement-After-Break-of-Structure-.png)

In this guide I uncover the secrets of inducement after break of structure — the scenario where price moves through a BOS without sweeping the original inducement and a new inducement has to be marked.

As you may have noticed, sometimes after a break of structure price does not sweep the inducement and continues its move — so:

**(I)** Should we wait for price to take the inducement created before the break of structure (BOS)?

**(II)** Will it create a new inducement?

**(III)** How do we identify the new inducement?

If you are new to my blog and the inducement concept, I recommend you first study [What is Inducement in Forex](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/what-is-inducement-in-forex/>) and then continue reading this article.

Before going toward the core concept of inducement after break of structure you should have knowledge about minor break of structure.

title: inducement-after-break-of-structure
section: What is Minor Break of Structure?
content:
#### What is Minor Break of Structure?

**(I) In Bullish Market**

After a major break of structure, when price moves up without sweeping the inducement and forms a [Swing High](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-high-explained/>), you have to wait for price to close above that swing high.

![Minor break of structure in a bullish market — price closes above the new swing high without sweeping the original inducement, shifting the high while the rest of the structure stays unchanged](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Untitled.png)

This scenario, known as a minor break of structure, results in a shift of the price high while the rest of the market structure remains unchanged.

**(II) In Bearish Market**

After a major break of structure, when price moves down without sweeping the inducement and forms a [Swing Low](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-low-formation/>), you need to wait for price to close below that swing low.

This scenario results in a shift of the price low while the rest of the market structure remains unchanged.

title: inducement-after-break-of-structure
section: What is Inducement after Break of Structure?
content:
#### What is Inducement after Break of Structure?

As discussed earlier, price sometimes continues its move after a break of structure and does not pull back to sweep the inducement.

In this scenario, if we wait for price to sweep the first inducement, we will not get a trading opportunity at all.

So we wait for price to create a new inducement and then grab it.

After that we can look for a trading opportunity, and the structural highs and lows will also be confirmed.

title: inducement-after-break-of-structure
section: (I) Inducement after BOS in Bullish Market
content:
#### (I) Inducement after BOS in Bullish Market

In a bullish market structure, price makes [Higher High and Higher Low](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/higher-high-and-higher-low/>). When price breaks the previous high it is called a break of structure, and the [Valid Pullback](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/3-step-guide-to-master-valid-pullback/>) before the BOS level is marked as inducement.

But if price does not grab the original inducement and continues to move bullish, we wait for a minor break of structure to find a new inducement.

When a minor break of structure happens, mark the lowest low and highest high of the bullish price leg which broke the swing high.

Now find a [Valid Pullback](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/3-step-guide-to-master-valid-pullback/>) in that bullish price leg and it will be the inducement level.

![Bullish inducement after BOS example — minor break of structure marks a new bullish leg, and the valid pullback inside that leg becomes the new inducement to wait for](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Untitled.png)

In this way you can look for each new inducement whenever price moves up without sweeping the inducement.

title: inducement-after-break-of-structure
section: (II) Inducement after BOS in Bearish Market
content:
#### (II) Inducement after BOS in Bearish Market

In a bearish market structure, price makes [Lower High and Lower Low](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/lower-high-and-lower-low/>). When price breaks the previous low it is called a break of structure, and the valid pullback before the BOS level is identified as inducement.

If price continues to move bearish without grabbing the inducement, we wait for a minor break of structure to identify a new inducement.

When a minor break of structure occurs, mark the highest high and lowest low of the bearish price leg that broke the swing low.

Next, identify a [Valid Pullback](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/3-step-guide-to-master-valid-pullback/>) within that bearish price leg, which will serve as the inducement level.

![Bearish inducement after BOS example — minor break of structure on the bearish side marks a new bearish leg, and the valid pullback inside that leg becomes the new inducement](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/BEARISH-INDUCEMENT-AFTER-bos.png)

This approach allows you to look for each new inducement whenever price moves down without sweeping the previous inducement.

title: inducement-after-break-of-structure
section: Step-by-Step Inducement After BOS Trade Flow
content:
#### Step-by-Step Inducement After BOS Trade Flow

This is the exact sequence I run when the original inducement has not been swept after a major BOS.

  1. **Confirm the major BOS.** Higher-timeframe break above the previous high (bullish) or below the previous low (bearish).
  2. **Check for the original inducement sweep.** If price already swept the pre-BOS inducement, trade that instead — there is no need to wait for a new one.
  3. **Watch for price moving away without the sweep.** Bullish — price continues up and forms a new swing high. Bearish — price continues down and forms a new swing low.
  4. **Wait for the minor BOS.** Bullish — close above the new swing high. Bearish — close below the new swing low.
  5. **Mark the new bullish or bearish leg.** The lowest low to the highest high (bullish) or the highest high to the lowest low (bearish) of the leg that produced the minor BOS.
  6. **Find the valid pullback inside the leg.** That valid pullback is the new inducement.
  7. **Wait for the sweep of the new inducement.** Bullish — price dips below the new inducement low. Bearish — price spikes above the new inducement high.
  8. **Wait for confirmation.** A lower-timeframe MSS, fair value gap or order block formed after the sweep.
  9. **Enter on the retest.** Take the trade in the higher-timeframe direction at the post-sweep PD array.
  10. **Stop and target.** Stop beyond the swept inducement extreme. Target the next draw on liquidity (old high or low, relative equal level, or higher-timeframe FVG).

title: inducement-after-break-of-structure
section: Common Mistakes Around Inducement After BOS
content:
#### Common Mistakes Around Inducement After BOS

These are the recurring mistakes I see when traders first start tracking inducement after a break of structure.

  1. **Holding onto the original inducement when price has clearly moved on.** If price has already produced a minor BOS away from the original inducement zone, the original inducement is stale. Mark the new one.
  2. **Marking inducement before the minor BOS confirms.** The minor BOS — the close above the new swing high (or below the new swing low) — is what validates the new leg. Marking inducement during the leg, before the close confirms, leads to fake levels.
  3. **Picking the wrong pullback inside the new leg.** Use the FIRST valid pullback inside the new leg, not the deepest one and not the most recent one.
  4. **Trading without higher-timeframe alignment.** Inducement-after-BOS only matters when the higher-timeframe bias is intact. In a choppy higher timeframe, every minor BOS is just noise.
  5. **Confusing minor BOS with full reversal.** A minor BOS shifts the high or low, it does not change the trend. The trend is still defined by the major structure.
  6. **Tight stops at the inducement itself.** Stop must sit BEYOND the swept inducement extreme — not at the inducement level. Stops parked at the inducement get hunted on the second test.

title: inducement-after-break-of-structure
section: Best Timeframe for Inducement After BOS
content:
#### Best Timeframe for Inducement After BOS

Use the 15-minute timeframe to mark the new inducement and execute the trade. Use the 1-day and 4-hour for the higher-timeframe market structure context — without that context the minor BOS is just intraday noise and the framework collapses.

title: inducement-after-break-of-structure
section: FAQs about Inducement After Break of Structure
content:
#### FAQs about Inducement After Break of Structure

Brief answers to the questions readers ask most often about inducement after BOS.

**What is inducement after break of structure?**

Inducement after BOS is the new inducement level that gets created when price moves through a major BOS without sweeping the original inducement. The new valid pullback inside the leg that produced the minor BOS becomes the new inducement.

**What is a minor break of structure?**

A minor BOS is a close above a new swing high (in a bullish market) or below a new swing low (in a bearish market) that occurs after a major BOS without the original inducement being swept. It shifts the price high or low while the rest of the market structure remains unchanged.

**Why does price sometimes skip the original inducement?**

When the algorithmic delivery is already pricing into a higher-timeframe draw on liquidity, it does not need to sweep the original inducement first. The move bypasses the original inducement and continues — which is exactly when the new inducement framework comes in.

**Should I still wait for the original inducement to be swept?**

Only if price stays inside the original BOS zone. Once price has produced a minor BOS away from the original inducement, the original level is stale — wait for the new inducement instead.

**Where is the new inducement after a minor BOS?**

It is the valid pullback inside the new bullish or bearish leg that produced the minor BOS. Mark the lowest low to highest high (bullish) or highest high to lowest low (bearish) of that leg, then find the first valid pullback inside it.

**Does this concept work on indices and gold?**

Yes — NQ, ES and XAU/USD all produce textbook minor-BOS-and-new-inducement patterns, especially during the New York AM session and around US economic releases.

**What timeframe is best?**

15-minute for marking and execution. 1-day and 4-hour for the higher-timeframe market structure context.

**What is the difference between the original inducement and the inducement after BOS?**

The original inducement is the valid pullback before the major BOS. The inducement after BOS is the valid pullback inside the leg that produced the minor BOS — it only exists when the original inducement has not been swept.

**How do I avoid this becoming an infinite chain?**

Each new minor BOS produces a new inducement. If the new inducement is also not swept and another minor BOS follows, repeat the process. The chain only ends when the inducement is finally swept and the algorithm delivers the real move.

It is important to mention that while market structure can provide valuable insights, it is not foolproof and should be used in conjunction with other technical analysis tools. Market conditions can change rapidly, so it is essential to consider other factors before making trading decisions and always use a stop loss to keep your equity safe.

# ICT Killzone and ICT Silver Bullet Overlap Strategy: Finding High-Probability Trade Setups

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/killzone-silver-bullet-overlap/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/killzone-silver-bullet-overlap/)

![ICT Killzone and Silver Bullet overlap diagram showing the London and New York windows where a Silver Bullet session falls inside an active Killzone](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/killzone-silver-bullet-overlap.png)

The ICT Killzones and the ICT Silver Bullet are two of the most popular concepts in the entire ICT method. On their own, each one helps a trader isolate the windows of the day when liquidity is deepest and institutional activity is highest. Most traders study them separately and never connect the two.

That separation is a missed edge. When I look at my own results, the cleanest setups almost always appear at one specific moment — when a Silver Bullet session falls entirely inside an active Killzone. That is the overlap, and it is where the two models reinforce each other instead of competing.

This guide is the complete explainer for the ICT Killzone and Silver Bullet overlap — what each concept is, where the two overlaps occur during the day, the step-by-step trade flow I run on each one, the common mistakes I see traders make, and the questions I get asked most often. If you are new to either concept, read the dedicated [ICT Killzones](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/master-ict-kill-zones/>) and [ICT Silver Bullet](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-silver-bullet-strategy/>) guides first, then come back here for the overlap.

title: killzone-silver-bullet-overlap
section: What Are ICT Killzones?
content:
#### What Are ICT Killzones?

ICT Killzones are fixed windows of the trading day when volume and volatility are at their highest, which is exactly when the highest-quality trading opportunities appear. Outside these windows, price often drifts and chops; inside them, institutions move with intent.

There are four Killzones, each named after the session that drives it. The times below are in New York local time:

  * **ICT Asian Killzone** — 07:00 PM to 10:00 PM
  * **ICT London Killzone** — 02:00 AM to 05:00 AM
  * **ICT New York Killzone** — 07:00 AM to 09:00 AM
  * **ICT London Close Killzone** — 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM

For the full breakdown of every session, see the complete [ICT Killzones guide](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/master-ict-kill-zones/> "ICT Killzones — All 4 Sessions \(Asian, London, NY, London Close\) Times + Trading Guide").

title: killzone-silver-bullet-overlap
section: What Is the ICT Silver Bullet?
content:
#### What Is the ICT Silver Bullet?

The ICT Silver Bullet is a time-based algorithmic trading model built on [liquidity](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/liquidity-in-forex-trading/>) and the [Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/fair-value-gap-trading-strategy/>). Unlike a Killzone, which is a broad window, the Silver Bullet is a precise one-hour entry model that repeats at the same three times every trading day.

The Silver Bullet appears three times each session, in New York local time:

  * **London Silver Bullet** — 03:00 AM to 04:00 AM
  * **New York AM Silver Bullet** — 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM
  * **New York PM Silver Bullet** — 02:00 PM to 03:00 PM

For the complete setup, see the full [ICT Silver Bullet strategy guide](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-silver-bullet-strategy/> "Master ICT Silver Bullet Strategy — Times, Setup").

title: killzone-silver-bullet-overlap
section: ICT Killzone and Silver Bullet Overlap
content:
#### ICT Killzone and Silver Bullet Overlap

An overlap occurs when the one-hour Silver Bullet window falls inside a wider Killzone window. During that hour, the market carries two layers of confluence at once — the deep liquidity and volatility of the Killzone, plus the precise, repeatable entry model of the Silver Bullet. In my experience, this combination produces cleaner price delivery, stronger displacement, and far more reliable Fair Value Gap reactions than either concept on its own.

The practical value of the overlap is that it works as a filter. Instead of trading every Silver Bullet of the day, I only take the Silver Bullet setups that form during an active Killzone. That single rule removes most of the low-quality, mid-session noise and concentrates my risk on the hours when institutional participation is highest.

There are two major overlaps worth trading — the **London overlap** and the **New York overlap**. Each one has its own window and its own personality, but the trade flow is identical.

title: killzone-silver-bullet-overlap
section: London Killzone and Silver Bullet Overlap
content:
#### London Killzone and Silver Bullet Overlap

The London overlap sits inside one of the most active periods of the entire trading day. The London Killzone runs from 02:00 AM to 05:00 AM, and the London Silver Bullet runs from 03:00 AM to 04:00 AM — fully contained inside it.

**Overlap window:** 03:00 AM to 04:00 AM New York time.

This hour frequently produces a liquidity sweep of the Asian session range before the market commits to the day’s direction. That sweep is the fuel for the setup — institutions trigger resting stop losses, fill their positions, and then drive price away with displacement.

title: killzone-silver-bullet-overlap
section: How to Trade the London Overlap
content:
#### How to Trade the London Overlap

This is the exact sequence I run on every overlap setup. Do not skip a step.

  1. **Establish your bias.** Before the overlap begins, decide whether the higher-timeframe narrative is bullish or bearish using [ICT Daily Bias](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-daily-bias-explained/>). Trade the overlap in the direction of that bias.
  2. **Wait for a liquidity sweep.** Inside the overlap window, let price raid an obvious liquidity pool — the Asian session high or low, the previous session high or low, an intraday swing point, or equal highs and equal lows. The sweep matters because institutions accumulate after taking out retail stops.
  3. **Look for a Market Structure Shift.** After the sweep, wait for a strong move that breaks short-term structure, leaves an obvious imbalance, and prints a Fair Value Gap. That displacement is your confirmation of institutional intent — see [ICT Market Structure Shift](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-market-structure-shift/>) for the full mechanic.
  4. **Enter on the Fair Value Gap retracement.** Once the FVG forms, wait for price to retrace back into it. The retracement tap is your entry, not the displacement candle itself.
  5. **Place your stop loss.** For a bullish setup, the stop sits below the liquidity sweep low. For a bearish setup, it sits above the liquidity sweep high.
  6. **Set your targets.** Aim for the next pool of liquidity — previous session liquidity, London liquidity, New York liquidity, or external liquidity. I want a minimum risk-to-reward of 1:2, and many of these setups deliver 1:3 or better.

The chart below shows a live London overlap. This setup formed on 12 June 2026 at 03:45 AM New York time. Price raided the previous low, gave a Market Structure Shift to the buy side, and I entered on the retracement into the Fair Value Gap, targeting the previous high for a 1:4 risk-to-reward.

![London Killzone and Silver Bullet overlap trade example — Asian-range liquidity sweep, MSS to the buy side, entry on the Fair Value Gap retracement, target at the previous high for 1:4](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/london-overlap.png)

title: killzone-silver-bullet-overlap
section: New York Killzone and Silver Bullet Overlap
content:
#### New York Killzone and Silver Bullet Overlap

The New York overlap forms later in the morning, after the initial New York volatility has already been established. The London Close Killzone runs from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM, and the New York AM Silver Bullet runs from 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM — contained inside it.

**Overlap window:** 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM New York time.

Because the morning move is already in play by this hour, the New York overlap often produces high-quality continuation setups, and sometimes sharp reversals when the morning push has run into a higher-timeframe level.

title: killzone-silver-bullet-overlap
section: How to Trade the New York Overlap
content:
#### How to Trade the New York Overlap

The trade flow for the New York overlap is identical to the London overlap above. Here is the condensed version.

First, set your bias before the overlap window opens. During the window, wait for price to sweep an important liquidity level — the Asian high or low, the previous session high or low, equal highs or lows, or an intraday swing point. After the sweep, look for a Market Structure Shift and a strong move that leaves a Fair Value Gap behind. Enter when price retraces back into that Fair Value Gap.

For bullish trades, place the stop loss below the liquidity sweep low. For bearish trades, place it above the liquidity sweep high. Target previous session liquidity, London liquidity, New York liquidity, or any external liquidity level in the direction of your bias.

The chart below shows a live New York overlap. This setup formed on 10 June 2026 during the New York AM Silver Bullet, inside the London Close Killzone. Price raided the previous high, gave a Market Structure Shift to the sell side, and I entered on the retracement into the Fair Value Gap, targeting the previous low for a 1:3 risk-to-reward.

![New York Killzone and Silver Bullet overlap trade example — previous-high liquidity sweep, MSS to the sell side, entry on the Fair Value Gap retracement, target at the previous low for 1:3](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/NEW-YORK-Overlap.png)

title: killzone-silver-bullet-overlap
section: Best Pairs and Timeframes for the Overlap
content:
#### Best Pairs and Timeframes for the Overlap

The overlap respects almost any liquid instrument, but it is cleanest where price delivery is tightest. I trade it on the US index futures and the major USD pairs, and I avoid low-volume, illiquid pairs where the sweep-and-displacement sequence is messy.

For execution, I mark the liquidity and bias on the 15-minute and 5-minute charts, then drop to the 3-minute or 1-minute inside the overlap window to time the Market Structure Shift and the Fair Value Gap entry. The higher timeframe gives the context; the lower timeframe gives the trigger.

title: killzone-silver-bullet-overlap
section: USA Trading Note — ES & NQ Futures
content:
#### USA Trading Note — ES & NQ Futures

For US-based traders, both overlaps print cleanest on US index futures — the **NASDAQ 100 (NQ Futures)** and the **E-mini S &P 500 (ES Futures)**. The New York overlap in particular lines up with peak CME futures activity, and the session structure produces the tight liquidity sweeps and sharp displacement these setups depend on. ES and NQ are CFTC-regulated futures and execute through a US futures broker such as NinjaTrader, AMP, Tradovate, or a prop firm like Topstep. The major USD pairs (EUR/USD, GBP/USD) and Gold (XAU/USD) also respect the overlap mechanics. TradingView is for chart analysis only.

title: killzone-silver-bullet-overlap
section: Common Mistakes I See Traders Make on the Overlap
content:
#### Common Mistakes I See Traders Make on the Overlap

A handful of repeatable errors account for most of the failed overlap trades I see in the comments. Avoid these and the model converts at a much higher rate.

  1. **Trading the Silver Bullet outside the Killzone.** The entire edge of the overlap is the confluence. A Silver Bullet that does not sit inside an active Killzone loses the liquidity backdrop that makes the setup work. If there is no overlap, there is no trade.
  2. **Entering before the liquidity sweep.** The sweep is the trigger, not an optional extra. Entering on the first move of the window, before institutions have taken out a liquidity pool, is how traders get caught on the wrong side of the displacement.
  3. **Skipping the bias step.** Counter-bias overlaps fail far more often than aligned ones. Decide the higher-timeframe narrative before the window opens, and only take setups in that direction.
  4. **Entering on the displacement candle instead of the retracement.** The entry is the retracement into the Fair Value Gap, not the impulse that created it. Chasing the displacement gives a terrible entry price and a stop loss that is too far away.
  5. **Forcing a trade when no clean setup forms.** Some overlap windows simply do not produce a sweep, a structure shift, and a Fair Value Gap. When the sequence is not clean, there is no trade. Patience is part of the model.

title: killzone-silver-bullet-overlap
section: Final Thoughts
content:
#### Final Thoughts

The Killzone and Silver Bullet overlap is one of the simplest filters you can add to your trading, and one of the most powerful. Rather than chasing every session, you wait for the one hour where deep liquidity and a precise entry model line up, then run the same sweep, shift, and Fair Value Gap sequence every time. Master the two overlaps and you remove most of the noise from your trading day. For the building blocks, revisit the [ICT Killzones](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/master-ict-kill-zones/>) and [ICT Silver Bullet](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-silver-bullet-strategy/>) guides.

title: killzone-silver-bullet-overlap
section: Frequently Asked Questions
content:
#### Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the ICT Killzone and Silver Bullet overlap?**

The overlap is the window where a one-hour ICT Silver Bullet session falls entirely inside a wider ICT Killzone. During that hour the market carries both the deep liquidity of the Killzone and the precise entry model of the Silver Bullet, which produces cleaner displacement and more reliable Fair Value Gap setups.

**What are the two main overlaps?**

The London overlap runs from 03:00 AM to 04:00 AM New York time, where the London Silver Bullet sits inside the London Killzone. The New York overlap runs from 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM New York time, where the New York AM Silver Bullet sits inside the London Close Killzone.

**How do I trade the overlap?**

Set your bias before the window, wait for a liquidity sweep inside the window, look for a Market Structure Shift that leaves a Fair Value Gap, and enter on the retracement into that gap. Stop loss goes beyond the sweep, and targets are the next pools of liquidity in the direction of your bias.

**Why is the overlap better than trading the Silver Bullet alone?**

The overlap acts as a filter. By taking only the Silver Bullet setups that form inside an active Killzone, you concentrate on the hours of highest institutional participation and remove most of the low-quality, mid-session signals.

**Where do I place my stop loss?**

Below the liquidity sweep low for a bullish setup, and above the liquidity sweep high for a bearish setup. The sweep extreme is the level institutions defended, so a stop beyond it gives the trade room while keeping risk defined.

**What timeframe is best for the overlap?**

Mark liquidity and bias on the 15-minute and 5-minute charts, then drop to the 3-minute or 1-minute inside the overlap window to time the Market Structure Shift and the Fair Value Gap entry. The higher timeframe gives context; the lower timeframe gives the trigger.

**Which instruments work best for the overlap?**

US index futures — the NASDAQ 100 (NQ) and E-mini S&P 500 (ES) — print the cleanest overlaps because of tight CME price delivery. The major USD pairs (EUR/USD, GBP/USD) and Gold (XAU/USD) also respect the mechanics. Avoid low-volume pairs where the sweep and displacement sequence is messy.

# Liquidity in Forex Trading — Buy-Side vs Sell-Side Liquidity Explained (ICT) + Free PDF

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/liquidity-in-forex-trading/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/liquidity-in-forex-trading/)

![Liquidity in Forex Trading — buy-side liquidity above old highs and sell-side liquidity below old lows where market makers hunt retail stops](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Liquidity-in-forex-trading.png)

Liquidity in forex trading is the availability of willing buyers and sellers at the market price. In ICT terms, it specifically refers to the pending buy stops resting above old highs (buy-side liquidity) and the pending sell stops resting below old lows (sell-side liquidity) — the pools that market makers target to fill institutional orders.

In this guide I walk you through the meaning of liquidity, the two types (buy-side vs sell-side), the liquidity hunt mechanic, why this is the primary driver of price, and how to read it like a pro.

Table of Contents

title: liquidity-in-forex-trading
section: What is Liquidity in Forex Trading?
content:
#### What is Liquidity in Forex Trading?

The word liquidity itself means convertible to cash.

The liquidity of an asset is marked high if it can easily be sold and converted to cash.

In forex trading, liquidity means the availability of willing buyers and sellers at the market price. If someone wants to buy an asset there should be a seller of that asset, and for a seller there should be a buyer.

Liquidity makes it easy for the market to operate effectively.

Liquidity in the forex market is measured by the volume of active or pending orders in the market. Market makers mostly try to hunt the liquidity of retail traders — and that hunt is the engine of price delivery.

title: liquidity-in-forex-trading
section: Types of Liquidity in Trading
content:
#### Types of Liquidity in Trading

As there are two types of orders in trading — buy and sell — liquidity is also of two types: **buy-side** and **sell-side**.

title: liquidity-in-forex-trading
section: Buy-Side Liquidity (ICT)
content:
#### Buy-Side Liquidity (ICT)

**Buy-side liquidity** , according to the inner circle trader (ICT), is the volume of pending buy orders (buy stops).

When traders execute a sell order they often want to protect it with a buy order in case price moves against them.

So they use a buy stop to protect their capital and hedge against loss.

Anyone selling at a price level will have a buy stop placed above that price.

So buy stops rest above highs — and that is why old highs like weekly highs, daily highs or equal highs are termed buy-side liquidity.

Market makers try to grab these highs to convert the pending orders into market orders, and then move the market against them.

In this way they make profit from retail traders, and this is termed a **liquidity hunt**.

![Buy-side liquidity hunt — market makers sweep equal highs above old highs and reverse the market lower against the buy stops](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Liquidity-Hunt.png)

In the picture above you can see equal highs that are termed buy-side liquidity. Market makers swept the old highs clearing buy-side liquidity, then moved the market down against the pending orders — a perfect example of a buy-side liquidity hunt.

title: liquidity-in-forex-trading
section: Sell-Side Liquidity (ICT)
content:
#### Sell-Side Liquidity (ICT)

**Sell-side liquidity** , as defined by the Inner Circle Trader (ICT), refers to the accumulation of pending sell orders — particularly sell stop orders.

When traders initiate buy orders, they often seek to safeguard their positions by placing corresponding sell orders to mitigate potential losses.

Sell stop orders serve as a protective mechanism, activated if the price declines beyond a certain threshold.

Typically, traders position sell stop orders below significant price levels — such as historical lows, including weekly lows, daily lows or equivalent benchmarks.

These levels are deemed to contain sell-side liquidity due to the concentration of pending sell orders.

Market makers attempt to exploit this liquidity by targeting these established lows to trigger the activation of sell stop orders, effectively converting them into market orders.

Subsequently, they capitalise on this influx of market orders to manipulate the market in the opposite direction, thereby profiting from the actions of retail traders.

In essence, the concept of sell-side liquidity underscores the strategic interplay between traders and market makers, with sell stop orders serving as pivotal instruments in this dynamic process.

![Sell-side liquidity hunt — market makers sweep below established lows clearing sell stops and then move the market upward into buy-side](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/sell-side-liquidity.png)

In the picture above you can see established lows with sell stops resting below them. Price after clearing the lows and sell-side liquidity moved into the buy side — a perfect example of a sell-side liquidity hunt.

title: liquidity-in-forex-trading
section: Buy-Side vs Sell-Side Liquidity (Side-by-Side)
content:
#### Buy-Side vs Sell-Side Liquidity (Side-by-Side)

The two types are mirror opposites. Use this side-by-side as a quick reference.

  * **Buy-side liquidity** — buy stops above old highs (weekly, daily, equal highs). Filled when price runs above the level. Market makers sweep it then sell into it, reversing lower.
  * **Sell-side liquidity** — sell stops below old lows (weekly, daily, equal lows). Filled when price runs below the level. Market makers sweep it then buy into it, reversing higher.

The most important practical rule: in a bullish higher-timeframe bias, expect price to sweep sell-side liquidity (below an old low) before continuing up. In a bearish higher-timeframe bias, expect price to sweep buy-side liquidity (above an old high) before continuing down.

title: liquidity-in-forex-trading
section: Why Understanding Liquidity is Important
content:
#### Why Understanding Liquidity is Important

By the discussion above you have understood the meaning and types of liquidity in forex trading, and you also know that market makers look to hunt liquidity.

The market, after hunting liquidity on one side, moves to hunt the liquidity on the other side — as you can see in the picture below.

![Liquidity grab — market makers hunt one side of liquidity then rotate to hunt the opposite side, the engine of price delivery](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/liquidity-grab.png)

So liquidity is the primary cause of price movement.

As a trader, if you do not know about liquidity in the market, you can become the liquidity yourself. To be a profitable trader you should know and spot the liquidity in the market and try to go with the flow of market makers.

title: liquidity-in-forex-trading
section: Step-by-Step Liquidity-Reading Workflow
content:
#### Step-by-Step Liquidity-Reading Workflow

This is the exact sequence I run before any trading session to map liquidity correctly.

  1. **Set the higher-timeframe bias.** Daily and H4 — bullish, bearish or neutral.
  2. **Mark the previous day high and previous day low.** The most recent buy-side and sell-side pools.
  3. **Mark the previous week high and low.** The next-tier pools above and below.
  4. **Mark relative equal highs and lows.** Internal liquidity inside the range.
  5. **Identify the next draw-on-liquidity.** Above (buy-side) or below (sell-side) — guided by the bias.
  6. **Wait for the sweep.** Price must wick through the level and close back inside the prior range.
  7. **Confirm with structure.** A lower-timeframe Market Structure Shift after the sweep is the trigger.
  8. **Take entry, stop and target.** Entry on the retest of the PD array, stop beyond the swept level, target the opposite-side pool.

title: liquidity-in-forex-trading
section: Best Markets for Reading Liquidity
content:
#### Best Markets for Reading Liquidity

Liquidity is universal across markets, but the cleanest signatures print on a specific subset.

  * **NQ (NASDAQ futures)** and **ES (S &P 500 futures)** — institutional flow is concentrated, so buy-side and sell-side pools are unambiguous.
  * **GBP/USD** and **EUR/USD** — relative equal highs and lows form constantly during the London-NY overlap.
  * **XAU/USD (Gold)** — large stop runs around US economic releases (NFP, CPI) deliver textbook liquidity hunts.

**For traders in the United States** who follow the CFTC FIFO and no-hedge rules, the liquidity model maps directly onto NQ and ES futures (CME Group). The 09:50 NY-AM [macro window](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-macro-time-based-strategy/>) is a particularly strong place to read liquidity hunts because the algorithm is most active there. The model also maps onto regulated forex pairs through US-based brokers — the mechanic does not change, only the instrument.

title: liquidity-in-forex-trading
section: Common Mistakes Reading Forex Liquidity
content:
#### Common Mistakes Reading Forex Liquidity

These are the recurring mistakes I see when traders first start working with the liquidity framework.

  1. **Treating every old level as liquidity.** Only the meaningful, untouched levels matter — relative equal highs/lows, weekly highs/lows and prior day highs/lows.
  2. **Front-running the sweep.** Pre-positioning before price reaches the level removes the entire liquidity-hunt mechanic from your trade.
  3. **Confusing pool with sweep.** The [liquidity pool](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-liquidity-pool/>) is the resting orders. The [sweep](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-liquidity-sweep-vs-liquidity-run/>) is the action of taking them. Both terms are related but not identical.
  4. **No higher-timeframe context.** A buy-side sweep on a bearish daily is a setup for a continuation lower. The same sweep on a bullish daily is a continuation higher. Context decides the direction.
  5. **Over-trading liquidity sweeps.** Not every sweep is a setup. The cleanest sweeps come at structural extremes — not in the middle of the range.
  6. **Ignoring news.** A red-folder release inside the sweep window distorts price and routinely turns a clean read into a stop-out.

title: liquidity-in-forex-trading
section: FAQs about Liquidity in Forex Trading
content:
#### FAQs about Liquidity in Forex Trading

Brief answers to the questions readers ask most often about liquidity.

**What is liquidity in forex trading?**

Liquidity is the availability of willing buyers and sellers at the market price. In ICT terms, it specifically refers to the pending buy stops above old highs (buy-side) and the pending sell stops below old lows (sell-side) that market makers target.

**What is buy-side liquidity?**

Buy-side liquidity is the cluster of pending buy stops resting above weekly highs, daily highs or relative equal highs. It is the pool that market makers sweep when price breaks above an old high.

**What is sell-side liquidity?**

Sell-side liquidity is the cluster of pending sell stops resting below weekly lows, daily lows or relative equal lows. It is the pool that market makers sweep when price breaks below an old low.

**What is the difference between buy-side and sell-side liquidity?**

Buy-side liquidity sits above old highs (buy stops). Sell-side liquidity sits below old lows (sell stops). Market makers hunt the side that aligns with the next draw on liquidity, which is determined by the higher-timeframe bias.

**What is a liquidity hunt?**

A liquidity hunt is the action of market makers sweeping a pool of resting orders (above an old high or below an old low) to convert pending stops into market orders, then moving price against those orders to fill the institutional position.

**Why is liquidity important in forex?**

Liquidity is the primary cause of price movement. The market rotates between hunting one side of liquidity and the other, so reading liquidity correctly tells you where price is most likely to go next.

**How is liquidity measured in forex?**

Liquidity in the forex market is measured by the volume of active and pending orders. ICT-style readers focus on the location of pending orders — buy stops and sell stops — rather than the absolute volume number.

**Where do buy stops rest in forex?**

Buy stops rest above weekly highs, daily highs and relative equal highs. These levels are the buy-side liquidity pools.

**Where do sell stops rest in forex?**

Sell stops rest below weekly lows, daily lows and relative equal lows. These levels are the sell-side liquidity pools.

**How do market makers hunt liquidity?**

Market makers run price through an old high or old low, triggering the resting stops, which become market orders that fill the institutional position. Once filled, price reverses against the just-triggered orders.

**What is liquidity in ICT?**

In ICT terminology, liquidity is the location of pending orders — buy-side above old highs and sell-side below old lows. The ICT framework treats liquidity as the primary cause of price delivery.

# Lower High and Lower Low — Identify Valid Bearish Market Structure with Inducement Sweep

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/lower-high-and-lower-low/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/lower-high-and-lower-low/)

Lower High and Lower Low are the two building blocks of bearish market structure — but not every visible low or high qualifies as STRUCTURAL. The valid lower low requires an inducement sweep, and the valid lower high requires both an inducement sweep AND a follow-up break of structure to confirm.

In this guide I walk you through the identification of lower high and lower low — the inducement-sweep rule, the swing-formation sequence, the structural high and low after a bearish CHOCH, common mistakes and the FAQ. For the bullish mirror see my [Higher High and Higher Low](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/higher-high-and-higher-low/>) guide.

After studying this article and spending time in practice you will gain the ability to identify lower high and lower low like a pro.

**(I)** [Market Structure](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/market-structure-in-trading/>)

title: lower-high-and-lower-low
section: How to Identify Lower Low in Bearish Trend
content:
#### How to Identify Lower Low in Bearish Trend

In a bearish trend, price makes lower lows — but every low is not a valid structural low.

To identify a valid lower low in a bearish trend, you have to identify [Inducement](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/what-is-inducement-in-forex/>) first.

After identifying the inducement, wait for price to make a [Swing Low](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-low-formation/>) and retrace up to sweep the inducement.

When price sweeps the inducement, the last swing low formed BEFORE sweeping the inducement is marked as the valid lower low.

![Lower low identification example — inducement marked, swing low forms, price sweeps the inducement, then the last swing low is confirmed as the valid lower low](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/lower-low.png)

When price breaks below the lower low, it is called a valid break of structure.

Every time price breaks the structure to the downside, you have to look for the inducement sweep to confirm the lower low.

title: lower-high-and-lower-low
section: How to Identify Lower High in Bearish Trend
content:
#### How to Identify Lower High in Bearish Trend

In a bearish trend, price makes lower highs — but every high is not a valid lower high.

To confirm a high as a valid lower high, follow the steps explained below.

When price sweeps the inducement and confirms the lower low, look for the formation of a [Swing High](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-high-explained/>).

After the formation of the swing high, if price moves down and breaks the previous low, then the last swing high formed at the liquidity sweep is marked as the valid lower high.

![Lower high identification example — after inducement sweep and lower low confirmation, swing high forms, price breaks the previous low confirming the valid lower high](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/lower-high.png)

Every time after a break of structure to the downside, you have to look for a liquidity sweep and then the next break of structure to confirm a lower high.

title: lower-high-and-lower-low
section: How to Identify Structural High after Bearish CHOCH
content:
#### How to Identify Structural High after Bearish CHOCH

To identify a structural high after a bearish CHOCH, mark the last higher high that was made before the CHOCH.

The last higher high of the bullish trend is marked as the structural high when the market changes its trend from bullish to bearish — because the bearish trend starts from that high.

![Structural high after bearish CHOCH — last higher high of the prior bullish trend marked as the structural anchor for the new bearish leg](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/structural-high-1.png)

Then after every break of structure, look for an inducement sweep and a break of structure to the downside to confirm the lower high.

title: lower-high-and-lower-low
section: How to Identify Structural Low after Bearish CHOCH
content:
#### How to Identify Structural Low after Bearish CHOCH

[CHOCH](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/change-of-character-choch-in-trading/>) means change of character — and when the market changes its trend from bullish to bearish, you have to mark a lower low.

To identify a structural low after a bearish CHOCH, identify the inducement and wait for the formation of a swing low.

After the formation of the swing low, when price sweeps the inducement, the last swing low is marked as the valid structural low.

![Structural low after bearish CHOCH — first valid lower low marked after the change of character with inducement sweep confirming the structural anchor](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/structural-low-1.png)

As the trend is bearish, price will expectedly fall and break the previous low making a new low. After every break of structure, look for the inducement sweep to confirm the lower low.

title: lower-high-and-lower-low
section: Can We Mark a Lower Low Without an Inducement Sweep?
content:
#### Can We Mark a Lower Low Without an Inducement Sweep?

No — to confirm a lower low, the sweep of inducement is necessary.

If price breaks a low without sweeping the inducement, it is called a “Minor Break of Structure” — your low just shifts, but the overall market structure remains the same.

title: lower-high-and-lower-low
section: Can We Mark a Lower High Without an Inducement Sweep?
content:
#### Can We Mark a Lower High Without an Inducement Sweep?

No — to confirm a lower high, both the inducement sweep AND a break of structure to the downside are crucial.

Without the inducement sweep and a break of structure to the downside, you cannot mark a lower high.

title: lower-high-and-lower-low
section: Step-by-Step Lower High / Lower Low Identification
content:
#### Step-by-Step Lower High / Lower Low Identification

This is the exact sequence I run to mark every valid lower high and lower low in a bearish leg.

  1. **Confirm the bearish trend.** Either a fresh bearish CHOCH or an existing bearish series of lower lows.
  2. **Mark the structural high.** Last higher high before the CHOCH (or the most recent confirmed lower high if mid-trend).
  3. **Wait for the first swing low.** The next visible low in the bearish leg.
  4. **Mark the inducement.** The first valid pullback inside the leg toward that swing low — the inducement high.
  5. **Wait for the inducement sweep.** Price retraces up and spikes above the inducement high.
  6. **Confirm the lower low.** The last swing low formed BEFORE the inducement sweep is the valid lower low.
  7. **Wait for the BOS below that lower low.** A clean break below the lower low.
  8. **Confirm the lower high.** The last swing high formed at the inducement sweep is now the valid lower high.
  9. **Repeat for the next leg.** Each new bearish leg follows the same inducement-sweep-then-BOS sequence.
  10. **Watch for a bullish CHOCH.** The bearish series ends when price breaks the most recent lower high — that is the CHOCH that flips the bias.

title: lower-high-and-lower-low
section: Best Pairs for Lower High / Lower Low Trading
content:
#### Best Pairs for Lower High / Lower Low Trading

The structural-read framework works on every major instrument — GBP/USD, EUR/USD, USD/CAD, plus metals such as XAU/USD and XAG/USD, and indices like NQ and ES.

**For traders in the United States** who follow the CFTC FIFO and no-hedge rules, the lower-high / lower-low framework maps cleanly onto NQ and ES futures (CME Group) plus regulated forex pairs through US-based brokers. title: lower-high-and-lower-low
section: Common Mistakes Around Lower High and Lower Low
content:
#### Common Mistakes Around Lower High and Lower Low

These are the recurring mistakes I see when traders first start working with lower highs and lower lows.

  1. **Marking every visible low as a lower low.** Only the swing low BEFORE an inducement sweep qualifies. Random lows are noise.
  2. **Marking a lower high before the BOS.** The lower high is only confirmed AFTER the next break of structure to the downside. Marking it earlier creates false structure.
  3. **Confusing minor BOS with valid BOS.** Breaking a low without an inducement sweep is a minor BOS — the low just shifts. It is NOT a valid lower low.
  4. **Skipping the structural high / low anchor.** After a CHOCH, the prior trend’s last extreme becomes the structural anchor. Without it, you have no reference for the new trend.
  5. **Trading lower lows on the wrong timeframe.** A lower low on the 5-minute against a bullish daily is unreliable. Use top-down alignment.
  6. **Ignoring the inducement after CHOCH.** The first valid lower low after a CHOCH still requires inducement sweep — do not skip it because it is the first leg.

title: lower-high-and-lower-low
section: FAQs about Lower High and Lower Low
content:
#### FAQs about Lower High and Lower Low

Brief answers to the questions readers ask most often about lower highs and lower lows.

**What is a lower low in trading?**

A lower low is the structural low of a bearish leg — the last swing low formed BEFORE price sweeps the inducement. Breaking below it is the valid bearish break of structure.

**What is a lower high in trading?**

A lower high is the structural high of a bearish leg — the last swing high formed at the inducement sweep, confirmed when price then breaks the previous lower low to the downside.

**How is a lower low different from a swing low?**

Every swing low is a visible local extreme. A lower low is the SPECIFIC swing low that exists before an inducement sweep — the only one that counts as structural.

**Can I mark a lower low without inducement?**

No — without the inducement sweep, breaking a low is just a minor BOS. The low shifts but the structure does not advance.

**Can I mark a lower high without a BOS?**

No — the lower high requires BOTH the inducement sweep AND a follow-up break of structure to the downside to confirm. Without the BOS, the swing high is not yet structural.

**What is the structural high after a bearish CHOCH?**

The last higher high of the prior bullish trend — that is where the new bearish trend starts. It anchors all the lower highs that follow.

**What is the structural low after a bearish CHOCH?**

The first valid lower low after the CHOCH — confirmed by the inducement sweep on the new bearish leg.

**Is the market structure method reliable for trading?**

Yes — market structure is the most reliable method for trading. If you learn it properly and mark the structure accurately, it will produce great results.

**Can I trade using market structure alone?**

Yes — if you master market structure properly, you do not need any other indicator. You can trade the bearish trend using only the lower-high / lower-low sequence plus the inducement-sweep rule.

**What ends the bearish series of lower highs and lower lows?**

A bullish CHOCH — when price breaks the most recent lower high. That is the structural signal the trend has flipped.

**What timeframe is best for marking lower highs and lower lows?**

Use top-down analysis. The 1-day and 4-hour for the macro structure, the 15-minute or 1-hour for the intraday structure, the 5-minute for execution.

**Does this work on indices and gold?**

Yes — NQ, ES and XAU/USD all produce textbook lower-high / lower-low sequences, especially in trending environments after a CHOCH.
