title: market-structure-in-trading
section: What is Market Structure in Trading?
content:
#### What is Market Structure in Trading?

Market structure in trading is the real price action of the market — including [swing highs](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-high-explained/>), [swing lows](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-low-formation/>) and [inducement](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/what-is-inducement-in-forex/>). It tells us whether the market is in a trend or ranging. If it is in a trend, market structure tells us whether the trend is bullish or bearish.

Using market structure we can decide whether it is a good market condition to trade or not. And market structure helps us trade reversals and continuations of the trend.

title: market-structure-in-trading
section: Types of Market Structure in Trading
content:
#### Types of Market Structure in Trading

On the basis of the trend of the market, structure has 3 major types — bullish, bearish and sideways.

title: market-structure-in-trading
section: (I) Bullish Market Structure
content:
#### (I) Bullish Market Structure

A bullish market structure in trading refers to a financial market where prices are generally rising or expected to rise — also known as a bullish trend.

In bullish market structure, prices make higher highs and higher lows by breaking the previous swing high — which is called [Break of Structure](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/break-of-structure-bos/>). Until price does not break its previous higher low, it is expected that the market will continue its bullish trend and will break the previous high.

As you know “trend is your friend” — so in a bullish market we look for buying opportunities, mostly after a break of structure. When price retraces down and takes the inducement, we opt to buy after confirmation.

![Bullish market structure example — series of higher highs and higher lows with each break of structure confirming continuation and inducement levels marked for re-entry](https://www.innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/bullish-market-structure.png)

title: market-structure-in-trading
section: (II) Bearish Market Structure
content:
#### (II) Bearish Market Structure

A bearish market structure in trading refers to a financial market where prices are generally falling or expected to fall — also known as a bearish trend.

In bearish market structure, prices make lower highs and lower lows by breaking the previous swing low — which is called break of structure. Until price does not break its previous lower high, it is expected that the market will continue its bearish trend and will break the previous low.

In a bearish market we look for selling opportunities, mostly after a break of structure. When price retraces up and takes the inducement, we opt to sell after confirmation.

![Bearish market structure example — series of lower highs and lower lows with each break of structure confirming continuation and inducement levels marked for re-entry](https://www.innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Bearish-Market-Structure.png)

title: market-structure-in-trading
section: (III) Sideways Market Structure
content:
#### (III) Sideways Market Structure

A sideways market structure — also known as a horizontal or ranging market — refers to a financial market where the price of an asset trades within a relatively narrow range without showing a clear trend in either direction.

In a sideways market, price moves horizontally, fluctuating between a certain swing high and swing low, creating a trading range.

This market condition is good for scalping on lower timeframes, but to do an intraday or swing trade using market structure you should wait for a break of structure for a clear direction of the market.

![Sideways market structure example — horizontal range between equal highs and equal lows where price oscillates without forming a directional trend](https://www.innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/sideways-market-structure.png)

title: market-structure-in-trading
section: Market Structure Hierarchy — STH, ITH, LTH
content:
#### Market Structure Hierarchy — STH, ITH, LTH

ICT teaches a structural hierarchy that lets you read multiple layers of market structure simultaneously.

**STH** — [Short Term High](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-high-explained/>). A swing high local extreme between two lower highs.

**ITH** — [Intermediate Term High](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-advance-market-structure/>). A high between two short-term highs.

**LTH** — Long Term High. A high with lower intermediate-term highs on both sides.

The same hierarchy applies to lows — STL, [ITL, LTL](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-stl-itl-ltl/>). Reading STH / ITH / LTH together is what separates a structural trader from one chasing every wick.

title: market-structure-in-trading
section: Best Timeframe to Identify Market Structure
content:
#### Best Timeframe to Identify Market Structure

Market structure appears across all timeframes, and different timeframes often display different market structures.

For example, while the overall market structure on the higher timeframe may be bullish, the lower timeframe structure may be bearish as the market pulls back, awaiting the influx of buyers to continue the higher-timeframe move.

Higher volume is represented on higher timeframes, which means more market participants and more reliable sentiment. This generally results in a more consistent market structure.

On lower timeframes, market structure can often be less predictable and choppy from highs to lows.

The best approach is to have a clear understanding of the market as a whole. This includes lower timeframe, medium timeframe and higher timeframe structure. Think about each timeframe and align the market structure as a top-down analysis.

title: market-structure-in-trading
section: Step-by-Step Market Structure Trade Flow
content:
#### Step-by-Step Market Structure Trade Flow

This is the exact sequence I run when reading market structure for a trade.

  1. **Set the higher-timeframe context.** 1-day and 4-hour structure — bullish, bearish or ranging.
  2. **Identify the structural extremes.** Mark the most recent ITH / ITL on the higher timeframe.
  3. **Wait for the BOS.** Bullish — break above the previous swing high. Bearish — break below the previous swing low.
  4. **Mark the inducement inside the BOS leg.** The first valid pullback inside the leg.
  5. **Wait for price to retrace and take the inducement.** Bullish — price dips below the inducement low. Bearish — price spikes above the inducement high.
  6. **Drop to the lower timeframe.** 5-minute or 15-minute for the entry trigger.
  7. **Wait for the lower-timeframe MSS.** A clean break in the bias direction at the swept inducement.
  8. **Enter on the post-MSS retest.** At the post-sweep PD array.
  9. **Set the stop.** Beyond the swept inducement extreme, with a small buffer.
  10. **Take profit at the next draw on liquidity.** Old high or low, relative equal level, or higher-timeframe FVG.

title: market-structure-in-trading
section: Pros of Using Market Structure in Trading
content:
#### Pros of Using Market Structure in Trading

Market structure provides a clear overview of current market conditions and trends, and it can help you catch good continuation and reversal trades. When using market structure, always look left, find the valid inducement, and execute a trade after confirmation when price grabs the inducement.

title: market-structure-in-trading
section: Cons of Using Market Structure in Trading
content:
#### Cons of Using Market Structure in Trading

The market can do anything at any given moment. Uncertainty must be embraced and accepted. While market structure provides clues, there are no guarantees in trading — and it only takes a moment to reverse the trend.

Market structure principles may appear quite simple, but the complex details can take many years to master.

title: market-structure-in-trading
section: Best Pairs for Market Structure Trading
content:
#### Best Pairs for Market Structure Trading

Market structure works on every major instrument — GBP/USD, EUR/USD, USD/CAD, plus metals such as XAU/USD and XAG/USD.

**For traders in the United States** who follow the CFTC FIFO and no-hedge rules, market structure analysis maps cleanly onto NQ and ES futures (CME Group) plus regulated forex pairs through US-based brokers. The 09:50 NY-AM [macro window](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-macro-time-based-strategy/>) is the highest-conviction window for structural trade triggers.

title: market-structure-in-trading
section: Common Mistakes Around Market Structure
content:
#### Common Mistakes Around Market Structure

These are the recurring mistakes I see when traders first start working with market structure.

  1. **Reading only one timeframe.** Market structure on the 15-minute against the daily is unreliable. Top-down analysis is mandatory.
  2. **Treating every wick as a structural break.** Both BOS and CHOCH require the candle to close beyond the level — wicks alone are stop hunts.
  3. **Confusing BOS with CHOCH.** BOS = continuation. CHOCH = reversal. Mixing them flips the trade direction.
  4. **Trading every higher high or lower low.** Use the structural hierarchy (STH / ITH / LTH) to filter — only the ITL / ITH-level breaks are high-conviction.
  5. **Trading sideways markets like trending markets.** A range needs scalp tactics, not BOS-based trend continuation.
  6. **Skipping the inducement.** Entering at the BOS without an inducement sweep produces frequent stop-outs. The inducement is what makes the BOS high-conviction.

title: market-structure-in-trading
section: FAQs about Market Structure in Trading
content:
#### FAQs about Market Structure in Trading

Brief answers to the questions readers ask most often about market structure.

**What is market structure in trading?**

Market structure is the real price action of the market — including swing highs, swing lows, breaks of structure and inducement. It tells you whether the market is trending (bullish or bearish) or ranging.

**What are the three types of market structure?**

Bullish (higher highs and higher lows), bearish (lower highs and lower lows), and sideways (horizontal range between a swing high and swing low).

**What is the best timeframe to identify market structure?**

Market structure appears on every timeframe. The best approach is top-down analysis — read the daily, 4-hour and 15-minute together for a complete picture. Higher timeframes give more reliable structure; lower timeframes give the entry trigger.

**How is market structure different from BOS or CHOCH?**

Market structure is the overall price action read. BOS and CHOCH are specific structural events INSIDE that structure — BOS confirms the existing trend continuing, CHOCH confirms the trend reversing.

**What is the difference between bullish and bearish market structure?**

Bullish — higher highs and higher lows, with each new BOS confirming continuation. Bearish — lower highs and lower lows, with each new BOS confirming continuation in the bearish direction.

**How do I trade a sideways market?**

Either scalp inside the range (sell at the range high, buy at the range low) or wait for a break of structure before taking a directional trade. Trying to BOS-trade a tight range produces fakeouts.

**Where do I place the stop loss?**

Beyond the swept inducement extreme — below the inducement low for buy trades, above the inducement high for sell trades — with a small buffer.

**Where do I take profit?**

The next draw on liquidity — old high or low, relative equal level, or the next higher-timeframe PD array.

**What is the structural hierarchy STH, ITH, LTH?**

STH = short-term high (a swing high). ITH = intermediate-term high (between two STHs). LTH = long-term high (with lower ITHs on both sides). The same applies to lows — STL, ITL, LTL.

**Does market structure work on indices and gold?**

Yes — NQ, ES and XAU/USD all respect the same market structure principles, especially during the New York AM session and around US economic releases.

**How long does it take to master market structure?**

Market structure principles look simple but the complex details (multi-timeframe alignment, inducement validity, structural hierarchy) take many years to master. Three to six months is enough to use it profitably; full mastery takes longer.

**Can I trade with market structure alone?**

You can — but pairing market structure with PD arrays (FVG, OB, breaker) and time-based filters (killzones) produces a much higher hit rate than market structure alone.

# Master ICT 1st Presented Fair Value Gap and ICT Opening Range 2025

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/master-ict-1st-presented-fvg/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/master-ict-1st-presented-fvg/)

![ICT 1st Presented Fair Value Gap forming at the 9:30 AM New York opening range on a 1-minute chart](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/ICT-1st-Presented-FVG-1.png)

The first time I saw price snap back to the very first FVG of the New York session and reverse like a wall, I stopped trading the rest of the morning the same way. The 1st Presented FVG is the imbalance Smart Money sets in the first thirty minutes of the US session — and price respects it for the rest of the day.

The **ICT 1st Presented Fair Value Gap** is basically the very first FVG formed after the market opening at 09:30 AM New York local time. It acts as a catalyst for price movement on either side in a sideways market and supports the trend when the market is already moving in one direction. You can use the 1st presented FVG as a PD-Array to execute the trade.

In this guide, I will show you what the ICT Opening Range and Opening Range Gap are, how to identify the 1st Presented FVG correctly, the rule for qualifying or disqualifying it, and how to use it as a focal point for the entire NY session.

If you are brand new to fair value gaps, start with the foundational [ICT Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/fair-value-gap-trading-strategy/> "ICT Fair Value Gap") guide and come back here for the opening-range variant.

Do not worry — once the timing is set, this is a mechanical setup.

Ready? Let us break it down.

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: What is the ICT 1st Presented Fair Value Gap?
content:
## What is the ICT 1st Presented Fair Value Gap?

The ICT 1st Presented FVG is the very first fair value gap that forms at the opening, between 09:30 AM and 10:00 AM New York local time. It can either be a bullish FVG or a bearish FVG.

You would observe the 1-Minute chart to look for the 1st presented fair value gap, while the 5-Minute and 15-Minute charts are used for trading.

The 09:31 AM candlestick is the earliest where the imbalance part of this first presented fair value gap can be created.

![ICT 1st Presented FVG example: the very first fair value gap forming on the 1-minute chart between 9:30 and 10:00 AM New York time](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/ICT-1st-presented-FVG.png)

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: Why the 1st Presented FVG Matters
content:
## Why the 1st Presented FVG Matters

The 1st Presented FVG matters because it is the institutional fingerprint of the New York session. The first imbalance after the cash open marks where Smart Money committed price the moment the most active session of the day began.

For the rest of the trading day, that imbalance acts as a focal point. On a sideways day, price uses the 1st FVG as a magnet — pulling back to it from either side. On a trendy day, the 1st FVG acts as a continuation level — price pauses there and resumes in the direction of the trend.

If you are looking for one level to anchor your entire NY session, this is it.

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: What is the ICT Opening Range?
content:
## What is the ICT Opening Range?

The ICT Opening Range refers to the dynamic range of time starting at 09:30 AM New York local time and ending at 10:00 AM New York local time. It is called the Opening Range because the US stock market opens at 09:30 AM.

![ICT Opening Range example: the 30-minute window from 9:30 AM to 10:00 AM New York time marked on a price chart](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/ICT-Opening-Range.png)

This thirty-minute window is the only window in which the 1st Presented FVG is valid. Any FVG that prints after 10:00 AM is not the “1st presented” — it is just another FVG inside the broader session.

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: What is the ICT Opening Range Gap?
content:
## What is the ICT Opening Range Gap?

An ICT Opening Range Gap is the price difference between the previous day’s closing at 04:14 PM NY local time and the next day’s opening at 09:30 AM NY local time.

![ICT Opening Range Gap example: the price difference between previous day's 4:14 PM close and next day's 9:30 AM open marked on a chart](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/ICT-Opening-Range-Gap.png)

The Opening Range Gap is a separate concept from the 1st Presented FVG, but the two often appear together — the gap creates the displacement that produces the 1st FVG inside the opening range.

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: How to Qualify or Disqualify a 1st Presented FVG
content:
## How to Qualify or Disqualify a 1st Presented FVG

Not every fair value gap that prints between 09:30 and 10:00 AM is the real 1st Presented FVG. The qualification rule is mechanical:

**Qualified:** When the 1st fair value gap forms after 09:30 AM NY local time, look at the previous candlesticks before the FVG. If the FVG candlestick breaks the range of the previous candlesticks, then it is the real inefficiency and a qualified 1st presented fair value gap.

**Disqualified:** If the FVG candlestick does not break the previous candlesticks’ range, then it is not a real inefficiency. It is a disqualified 1st presented fair value gap and should be skipped.

Examples of both qualifications side by side:

![Disqualified 1st Presented FVG example: the FVG candlestick does not break the previous candlesticks' range](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Screenshot-33-1.png)

![Qualified 1st Presented FVG example: the FVG candlestick breaks the previous candlesticks' range, confirming the real inefficiency](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Screenshot-34.png)

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: How to Trade the 1st Presented FVG
content:
## How to Trade the 1st Presented FVG

Once you have a qualified 1st Presented FVG, the trade flow is straightforward:

  1. **Identify the 1st Presented FVG on the 1-minute chart** between 09:30 AM and 10:00 AM NY time.
  2. **Confirm qualification** — the FVG candlestick must break the range of the previous candlesticks.
  3. **Mark the FVG and extend it forward** through the whole day until 03:45 PM NY local time.
  4. **Switch to a 5-minute or 15-minute chart for execution.**
  5. **Wait for price to return to the 1st Presented FVG** during the day. On a trendy day, the FVG acts as a focal point — price often refers to it before continuing in the direction of the trend.
  6. **Enter on the reaction** — directly on tap, or with a lower-timeframe [CISD or MSS](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-cisd-and-ict-mss/> "ICT CISD vs MSS") confirmation for tighter entries.
  7. **Place stop loss** just beyond the far side of the 1st FVG.
  8. **Target** the next opposing PD Array or the next significant liquidity pool inside the day’s range.

The 1st Presented FVG can also be used as an [Inverse Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-inversion-fair-value-gap/> "Inverse Fair Value Gap") for trade opportunities — when price breaks through the FVG instead of holding it, the FVG flips role and becomes a continuation signal in the opposite direction.

**Pro Tip** — The strongest 1st Presented FVG trades happen when the FVG sits inside a higher-timeframe [PD Array](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-pd-array-key-to-trade-execution/> "ICT PD Array") — a daily fair value gap, an order block, or a breaker block. The intraday 1st FVG plus the higher-timeframe institutional level gives you confluence that holds with conviction. Skip 1st FVGs that print on news days during the first thirty minutes — the volatility distorts the imbalance and the level rarely respects.

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: Bonus Tip: Pairing With Daily Bias
content:
## Bonus Tip: Pairing With Daily Bias

Before the 9:30 AM New York open, set your [daily bias](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-daily-bias-explained/> "ICT Daily Bias"). If the bias is bullish, watch for a bullish 1st Presented FVG to act as a continuation level. If the bias is bearish, watch for a bearish 1st Presented FVG to act as a continuation short level.

If the 1st Presented FVG forms in the opposite direction of your daily bias, treat it with caution — it may be a fakeout that price uses to grab liquidity before reversing back into the bias direction. The Opening Range becomes a manipulation window, not a continuation window.

For more on validating fair value gaps before trading them, see our guide on the [Valid ICT Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/valid-ict-fair-value-gap/> "Valid ICT Fair Value Gap").

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: Frequently Asked Questions
content:
## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the ICT 1st Presented Fair Value Gap?

The ICT 1st Presented FVG is the very first fair value gap that forms after the New York stock market opens at 09:30 AM. It is identified on the 1-minute chart and traded on the 5-minute or 15-minute chart. It acts as a focal point for price during the rest of the trading day.

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: What time frame should I use to identify the 1st Presented FVG?
content:
### What time frame should I use to identify the 1st Presented FVG?

Use the 1-Minute chart to identify the 1st Presented FVG inside the opening range (9:30 to 10:00 AM NY time). Use the 5-Minute or 15-Minute chart for trade execution after the FVG is marked.

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: What is the earliest a 1st Presented FVG can form?
content:
### What is the earliest a 1st Presented FVG can form?

The 09:31 AM candlestick is the earliest at which the imbalance part of the 1st Presented FVG can be created. Anything before that is part of the gap from the previous session, not the 1st Presented FVG.

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: How do I qualify a 1st Presented FVG?
content:
### How do I qualify a 1st Presented FVG?

Look at the candlesticks before the FVG. If the FVG candlestick breaks the range of those previous candlesticks, the FVG is qualified — it represents a real inefficiency. If it does not break the prior range, the FVG is disqualified and should be skipped.

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: What is the difference between the Opening Range Gap and the 1st Presented FVG?
content:
### What is the difference between the Opening Range Gap and the 1st Presented FVG?

The Opening Range Gap is the price difference between the previous day’s 4:14 PM close and the next day’s 9:30 AM open. The 1st Presented FVG is the first three-candle fair value gap that forms inside the 9:30 to 10:00 AM opening range. They are related — the gap often produces the displacement that creates the FVG — but they are separate concepts.

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: Can I trade the 1st Presented FVG as an Inverse FVG?
content:
### Can I trade the 1st Presented FVG as an Inverse FVG?

Yes. If price breaks through the 1st Presented FVG instead of holding it, the FVG flips role and acts as an inverse — a continuation signal in the opposite direction. See our full guide on the Inverse Fair Value Gap for the mechanics.

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: How long should I keep the 1st Presented FVG marked on my chart?
content:
### How long should I keep the 1st Presented FVG marked on my chart?

Mark it and extend it through the whole day until 03:45 PM New York local time. Price refers back to it throughout the session, so the level remains active for most of the NY session.

title: master-ict-1st-presented-fvg
section: Wrapping Up
content:
## Wrapping Up

We hope this guide helped you understand the ICT 1st Presented Fair Value Gap and how to use it as the institutional anchor for your New York session.

The 1st FVG is one of the rare ICT setups with a fixed time window — 09:30 to 10:00 AM NY time, no exceptions. That precision is its edge. You either have it or you do not, and there is no second-guessing whether the level is valid.

This Monday, set an alert for the 9:30 AM New York open and watch the 1-minute chart. Mark the first qualified FVG you see. Then watch how price interacts with that level for the rest of the day.

ICT killzones refer to the hot trading hours in the forex markets with the most volatility and the best opportunities for profitable trading.

We all know the forex market operates 24 hours a day — but not all hours offer high volatility or the same favourable trading opportunities.

To address this and save traders time, Michael Huddleston came up with the idea of these 4 ICT killzones — the Asian killzone, London killzone, New York killzone and London close killzone.

In this guide I walk you through all 4 ICT killzones, their session times, the pairs that move best inside each one, the entry sequence I personally use and the common mistakes traders make when they first start trading the windows.

title: master-ict-kill-zones
section: What are ICT Killzones?
content:
#### What are ICT Killzones?

ICT killzones — also known as ICT session times or forex killzone times — are time frames with high trading volume and volatility in the market, resulting in good trading opportunities you can use to maximise profits.

These killzones are based on the four primary sessions of the international forex market: Sydney, Tokyo, London and New York. The overlap of these sessions and the institutional flow inside them is what makes the killzone windows volatile.

Another major factor contributing to the surge in trading volume during these sessions is heavy trade activity by various institutional traders, which Michael Huddleston refers to as ICT killzones.

These zones are divided into four time frames named: ICT Asian killzone, ICT London killzone, ICT New York killzone and ICT London close killzone. The timing for all four is tabulated below.

These ICT killzone times are referenced in both GMT and EST.

ICT Kill Zones| EST Time Frame| GMT Time Frame  
---|---|---  
ICT Asian Kill Zone| 07:00 PM – 10:00 PM| 12:00 AM - 03:00 AM  
ICT London Kill Zone| 02:00 AM – 05:00 AM| 07:00 AM - 10:00 AM  
ICT New York Kill Zone| 07:00 AM – 09:00 AM| 12:00 PM - 02:00 PM  
ICT London Close Kill Zone| 10:00 AM – 12:00 PM| 03:00 PM - 05:00 PM

  * Higher timeframe bias is helpful during this period, but a short-term retracement (bullish or bearish) can offer a similar optimal trade entry.

title: master-ict-kill-zones
section: Step-by-Step Killzone Trade Flow
content:
#### Step-by-Step Killzone Trade Flow

This is the exact sequence I run before any killzone window opens — from pre-market preparation to entry and management.

  1. **Set the daily bias.** Read the higher-timeframe [daily bias](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-daily-bias-explained/>) the night before — bullish, bearish or neutral.
  2. **Mark the draw on liquidity.** Highlight relative equal highs/lows, prior day high/low, prior session high/low and any unfilled fair value gaps.
  3. **Wait for the killzone to open.** Do not enter before the window. The institutional flow that creates the volatility starts only when the killzone opens.
  4. **Watch for the sweep.** The first move of the killzone is usually a liquidity sweep — Asian high/low for the London killzone, London high/low for the New York killzone, and so on.
  5. **Wait for an MSS.** A clean lower-timeframe market structure shift confirms intent.
  6. **Enter on the retracement.** Into the fair value gap, order block or OTE 0.62 to 0.79 zone left behind by displacement.
  7. **Set the stop.** Above the swept high (for shorts) or below the swept low (for longs), with a small buffer.
  8. **Take profit at the next external pool.** The opposite side of the prior session, relative equal highs/lows or the next day’s projected high/low.
  9. **Manage at first liquidity.** Move stop to break-even once the first internal pool is reached, then trail.

**For traders in the United States** who follow the CFTC FIFO and no-hedge rules, the New York killzone (07:00 to 10:00 AM ET) is the most natural fit — it overlaps with the open of the New York Stock Exchange at 09:30 ET and contains the 09:50 NY-AM macro window. NQ and ES futures (CME Group) along with major USD pairs deliver the cleanest setups inside this killzone.

title: master-ict-kill-zones
section: How does Daylight Saving Time Affect ICT Killzone Times?
content:
#### How does Daylight Saving Time Affect ICT Killzone Times?

Daylight Saving Time (DST) in the US is a practice where clocks are moved forward one hour in the spring, giving more daylight hours in the evening during the summer months, and then moved back one hour in the fall to return to standard time.

Essentially “springing forward” in March and “falling back” in November, with the time change occurring on the second Sunday of March and the first Sunday of November respectively, at 2:00 AM local time.

If your country does not follow daylight saving time then it can affect the ICT killzone times relative to your local time with a shift of an hour.

But if your country follows daylight saving time then you do not need to worry about it.

To avoid any confusion ICT himself recommends following the New York local time as the base time. It does not matter where you live — just follow the NY local clock.

The session and killzone windows remain the same irrespective of daylight saving; only the label changes from EST (Eastern Standard Time) to EDT (Eastern Daylight Saving Time).

title: master-ict-kill-zones
section: Common Mistakes When Trading ICT Killzones
content:
#### Common Mistakes When Trading ICT Killzones

These are the recurring mistakes I see when traders first start trading the killzone windows.

  1. **Pre-positioning before the window opens.** The killzone is the catalyst. An entry placed before the window opens removes the entire reason for using the strategy.
  2. **Trading every killzone.** Not every window has a clean draw on liquidity or a clean bias. If the higher-timeframe context is murky, sit out and wait for the next one.
  3. **Wrong pair for the wrong killzone.** Trying to trade GBP majors during the Asian killzone or AUD pairs during the New York killzone produces choppy, unreliable price action.
  4. **Ignoring the sweep.** The first leg of the killzone is usually a sweep, not the trade direction. Entering on the sweep itself almost always leads to a stop-out before the real move.
  5. **No MSS confirmation.** A market structure shift on the lower timeframe is the trigger. Without it the entry is guesswork.
  6. **Forgetting daylight saving.** Twice a year the EST/EDT label changes. If you trade from a fixed local clock, your entries will be off by an hour for two weeks until your charting platform syncs.
  7. **News overlap.** A red-folder release inside the killzone distorts price action. I avoid the window when high-impact news is scheduled inside it.

# ICT Liquidity Void — What It Is, How to Identify & Trade It + Free PDF

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/master-ict-liquidity-void/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/master-ict-liquidity-void/)

![ICT Liquidity Void — imbalance left behind when price breaks a consolidation and moves strongly in one direction without retracement, leaving multiple fair value gaps inside](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/ICT-Liquidity-Void-2.png)

A liquidity void is the imbalance left behind when price breaks a consolidation phase and moves strongly in one direction without retracement or wick overlap. It signals an absence of willing buyers or sellers in that price zone — and the algorithm typically returns to fill or partially reprice the void on a later leg.

In this guide I walk you through the ICT liquidity void — the meaning, the bullish and bearish identifications, the trade setup, the difference from a fair value gap, the common mistakes and the free PDF download.

title: master-ict-liquidity-void
section: What is an ICT Liquidity Void?
content:
#### What is an ICT Liquidity Void?

The word “liquidity” means willing buyers or sellers in the market. The word “void” means absence of something.

So an ICT liquidity void means the absence of buyers or sellers in the market — depending on the case.

When price breaks a consolidation phase and moves in one direction strongly without a retracement or wick inside the prior candlestick range, the imbalance created by those candlesticks is known as an ICT liquidity void.

Unlike a single 3-candle [fair value gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/fair-value-gap-trading-strategy/>), a liquidity void can span multiple consecutive candles and may contain two or more fair value gaps inside it.

title: master-ict-liquidity-void
section: Liquidity Void Meaning (Quick Definition)
content:
#### Liquidity Void Meaning (Quick Definition)

In ICT terminology, a **liquidity void** is a multi-candle imbalance zone created by a strong displacement move out of a consolidation. The void exists because there were no opposing orders to slow the move, so price covered the distance with no internal retracement. Price often returns later to reprice the void — partially or fully — before continuing in the original direction or reversing.

title: master-ict-liquidity-void
section: Bullish ICT Liquidity Void
content:
#### Bullish ICT Liquidity Void

A bullish liquidity void is created when price breaks the consolidation range and moves strongly to the buy side, targeting sell-side liquidity.

A bullish liquidity void is created by a [displacement move](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-displacement-move/> "Displacement Move"). Because of the absence of sell-side liquidity, price moves heavily to the buy side and creates the imbalance termed a bullish liquidity void.

![Bullish liquidity void diagram — strong displacement candles to the upside leaving multiple non-overlapping wick zones below](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/bullish-liquidity-void.png)

**To trade a bullish liquidity void** you have to look at the market structure to determine if it is bullish or bearish.

In a bullish market, price retraces back and fills the liquidity void, after which it continues going higher. So you can look for buy setups inside a bullish liquidity void.

A bullish liquidity void acts as a strong support in a bullish market, as you can see in the picture below.

![Bullish liquidity void trade example — price retraces into the void and respects it as support, then continues higher](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/bullish-liquidity-void-trading.png)

In a bearish market, bullish liquidity voids are not respected by price, and price will mostly continue going lower after repricing the liquidity void.

title: master-ict-liquidity-void
section: Bearish ICT Liquidity Void
content:
#### Bearish ICT Liquidity Void

When price breaks a consolidation range to the downside with strong momentum and large candles, targeting buy-side liquidity, it results in the formation of a bearish liquidity void.

It is formed because of the absence of buy-side liquidity — and price continues going lower without any retracement, making an imbalance known as a bearish liquidity void.

![Bearish liquidity void diagram — strong displacement candles to the downside leaving multiple non-overlapping wicks above](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/bearish-liquidity-void.png)

**To trade a bearish liquidity void** first identify the market structure.

If the market structure is bearish, price will retrace back and fill the liquidity void, after which it will continue going lower. You can look for sell setups inside a bearish liquidity void.

Bearish liquidity voids act as a strong resistance in a bearish market, as you can see in the picture below.

![Bearish liquidity void trade example — price retraces into the void and respects it as resistance, then continues lower](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/bearish-liquidity-void-trade.png)

If the market structure is bullish and a bearish liquidity void is created in a retracement move, then price may not respect the void and may continue higher even after repricing the bearish liquidity void.

title: master-ict-liquidity-void
section: Step-by-Step Liquidity Void Trade Flow
content:
#### Step-by-Step Liquidity Void Trade Flow

This is the exact sequence I run when trading a liquidity void.

  1. **Identify the higher-timeframe market structure.** Daily and H4 — bullish or bearish.
  2. **Spot the displacement move.** A strong directional break from a consolidation, large candles, no internal retracement.
  3. **Mark the liquidity void.** The price range covered by the displacement candles where wicks do not overlap.
  4. **Mark the consequent encroachment.** The 50% midpoint of the void — this is the most reactive level inside the imbalance.
  5. **Confirm bias alignment.** A bullish liquidity void in a bullish trend (or bearish in bearish trend) is high-probability. Counter-trend voids are not respected.
  6. **Wait for the retracement.** Price must trade back into the void.
  7. **Drop to the lower timeframe.** 5-minute or 15-minute for the entry trigger.
  8. **Wait for the LTF MSS.** A clean Market Structure Shift inside the void confirms the reaction.
  9. **Enter at the CE retest.** The 50% midpoint is the cleanest entry; a partial fill above or below is acceptable.
  10. **Set the stop.** Beyond the opposite edge of the void, or beyond the displacement candle’s high/low for tighter stops.
  11. **Take profit at the next draw on liquidity.** The opposite-side liquidity pool that the displacement was originally targeting.

title: master-ict-liquidity-void
section: Best Markets for Trading the Liquidity Void
content:
#### Best Markets for Trading the Liquidity Void

Liquidity voids form on every market that the ICT methodology is applied to.

  * **NQ (NASDAQ futures)** and **ES (S &P 500 futures)** — large displacement moves around the New York open and the 09:50 NY-AM macro produce textbook liquidity voids.
  * **XAU/USD (Gold)** — gold’s reaction to 08:30 ET news releases routinely creates large multi-candle voids that price reprices days later.
  * **GBP/USD** and **EUR/USD** — London-killzone displacement legs frequently leave voids on the way to the Asian-range sweep.

**For traders in the United States** who follow the CFTC FIFO and no-hedge rules, NQ and ES are the most natural fit for liquidity-void trading. The 09:50 NY-AM [macro window](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-macro-time-based-strategy/>) commonly produces the displacement that creates the void, and the same-day or next-day retest delivers the entry — fully accessible inside US working hours on the 1-minute and 5-minute charts.

title: master-ict-liquidity-void
section: Does a Liquidity Void Get Filled Instantly?
content:
#### Does a Liquidity Void Get Filled Instantly?

There is no fixed time for the repricing or filling of a liquidity void.

Price may fill a liquidity void instantly, or it may return to it after a few days.

You cannot force price — but you can wait for it. Whenever price reprices the liquidity void, you can look for your trade setup at that level.

title: master-ict-liquidity-void
section: Will Price Fill the Liquidity Void For Sure?
content:
#### Will Price Fill the Liquidity Void For Sure?

No — it is not necessary for price to fill every liquidity void.

Price may create another liquidity void and continue its move without filling the previous one. Some voids stay unfilled for weeks.

title: master-ict-liquidity-void
section: Will Price Fill the Liquidity Void Completely?
content:
#### Will Price Fill the Liquidity Void Completely?

Sometimes price may fill a liquidity void completely; sometimes it may not.

It is not necessary for price to fill a liquidity void completely. But you should wait for the [consequent encroachment](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-consequent-encroachment/> "Consequent Encroachment") (50% retracement) level of a liquidity void to be repriced before taking a trade. The 50% level is statistically the most reactive zone inside the void.

title: master-ict-liquidity-void
section: Liquidity Void vs Fair Value Gap
content:
#### Liquidity Void vs Fair Value Gap

An [ICT Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/fair-value-gap-trading-strategy/> "ICT Fair Value Gap") is a three-candle formation with a gap between the 1st and 3rd candlestick.

A liquidity void can be a formation of 3 or more candlesticks — and there can be 2 or more fair value gaps inside a single liquidity void.

In other words, the liquidity void is the broader imbalance container; the FVG is the discrete 3-candle unit. A void is “made of” FVGs, but the void itself is the displacement zone the algorithm tracks at a higher level.

title: master-ict-liquidity-void
section: Common Mistakes Around Liquidity Voids
content:
#### Common Mistakes Around Liquidity Voids

These are the recurring mistakes I see when traders first start trading liquidity voids.

  1. **Trading every void.** Voids that form against the higher-timeframe bias are not respected. Only trade voids in the direction of the daily and H4 trend.
  2. **Expecting full fills.** Many voids fill only to the 50% (consequent encroachment) before reversing. Waiting for a full fill misses most of the move.
  3. **Confusing voids with FVGs.** A 3-candle FVG is a single imbalance unit. A void is a multi-candle displacement zone. Trading them with the same expectations leads to wrong stop placement.
  4. **No LTF MSS at the retest.** The retest of the void is not the entry. The lower-timeframe Market Structure Shift inside the void is the trigger.
  5. **Stop too tight.** Stops parked at the CE often get hunted on the second test. The opposite edge of the void is the conservative stop.
  6. **Forgetting age.** Older voids may not get filled at all, especially after price has structurally moved past them. Voids printed in the same week or the same session are highest priority.

title: master-ict-liquidity-void
section: FAQs about ICT Liquidity Void
content:
#### FAQs about ICT Liquidity Void

Brief answers to the questions readers ask most often about the liquidity void.

**What is a liquidity void in trading?**

A liquidity void is the multi-candle imbalance left behind when price breaks a consolidation and moves strongly in one direction without internal retracement. It signals the absence of opposing orders in that price zone, and the algorithm typically returns to reprice the void on a later leg.

**What does liquidity void mean in forex?**

In forex (and on every market the ICT methodology is applied to), a liquidity void is the same concept — an imbalance zone created by a strong displacement move where no opposing liquidity slowed the move. The mechanic is identical to the indices and metals interpretation.

**How do I identify a liquidity void?**

Look for a strong directional break out of a consolidation, with multiple consecutive large-body candles whose wicks do not overlap the prior candle’s range. The price area covered by these displacement candles is the liquidity void.

**Will price always fill a liquidity void?**

No — price may create another void and continue without filling the previous one. Some voids stay unfilled for weeks. The probability of fill drops as price moves structurally further away.

**Where do I enter a liquidity void trade?**

After a higher-timeframe context confirms bias alignment and price retraces back into the void, wait for a lower-timeframe Market Structure Shift at the consequent encroachment (50%) of the void, then enter on the retest.

**Where do I place the stop loss?**

The conservative stop sits beyond the opposite edge of the liquidity void. Tighter stops can sit beyond the displacement candle’s high or low.

**Where do I take profit?**

The next draw-on-liquidity in the trend direction — typically the liquidity pool that the original displacement was targeting (the opposite side of the consolidation).

**What is the difference between liquidity void and fair value gap?**

A fair value gap is a single 3-candle gap. A liquidity void is a multi-candle zone that can contain two or more fair value gaps inside it. The void is the broader displacement container.

**Does the liquidity void work on indices and gold?**

Yes — NQ, ES and XAU/USD produce textbook liquidity voids around the New York AM session, the 09:50 macro and US economic releases.

**Does the liquidity void need to be filled before I can trade?**

No — you only need price to retrace back into the void to the consequent encroachment level before considering an entry. Full fills are not required.

**How long does it take to fill a liquidity void?**

There is no fixed time. Some voids fill within the same session; others stay unfilled for days or weeks. Recent voids (same week / same session) are the highest priority.

# Most Important ICT Concepts to Conquer the Market — Complete List

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list/)

![Most important ICT concepts complete list — liquidity, imbalance, displacement, market structure shift, order block, daily bias, premium and discount zones](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Most-Important-ICT-Concepts-.png)

ICT concepts are the trading techniques introduced by Michael Huddleston, also known as the Inner Circle Trader.

These concepts are based on the [Interbank Price Delivery Algorithm (IPDA)](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-ipda/>) which delivers price online.

By mastering these ICT concepts you can make your trades more successful.

This guide covers the basic understanding of each concept on a single page — to read any one of them in full, follow the link inside the section to the dedicated tutorial.

Table of Contents

[Toggle](<#>)

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Liquidity
content:
#### Liquidity

Liquidity is the base of price movement and the ICT concepts.

As ICT mentioned, price moves because of two main reasons — and one of them is liquidity.

Liquidity refers to the stop-loss orders and the pending buy or sell orders of market participants.

Liquidity is divided into two types: buy-side liquidity and sell-side liquidity.

Buy-side liquidity refers to the stop-loss orders of sellers and the buy-stop orders of waiting buyers.

Sell-side liquidity refers to the stop-loss orders of buyers and the sell-stop orders of waiting sellers.

On a price chart, liquidity resides at the crucial levels — strong support and resistance areas, relative equal highs and lows, or psychological price levels.

You can see the example of liquidity indicated on the price chart in the picture given below.

![ICT liquidity example — relative equal highs marked as buy-side liquidity, relative equal lows as sell-side liquidity, with smart money sweeping each pool before reversing](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/liquidity-grab.png)

Smart Money Concepts state that smart money knows about these levels of liquidity and tries to hunt the liquidity of retailers before moving price in their favor. ICT traders follow the footprints of smart money and make profits.

For the detailed study about liquidity, see my dedicated [Liquidity in Forex Trading](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/liquidity-in-forex-trading/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Imbalance (Fair Value Gap)
content:
#### Imbalance (Fair Value Gap)

Imbalance is the 2nd reason for price movement on the chart and is one of the bases of ICT concepts.

Imbalance refers to the disparity between buying and selling forces.

An imbalance is indicated by the [ICT Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/fair-value-gap-trading-strategy/>), which is a three-candle formation with a gap between the 1st and 3rd candle that remains unmitigated.

Price often refers back to these areas for the fair value, and these areas act as support or resistance for price.

You can see the example of a fair value gap in the picture below.

![ICT fair value gap example — three-candle imbalance with the gap between the 1st and 3rd candle marked as the unmitigated FVG zone](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/ICT-Fair-Value-Gap-1.png)

For the complete study about fair value gaps, see my dedicated [Fair Value Gap Trading Strategy](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/fair-value-gap-trading-strategy/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Displacement
content:
#### Displacement

Displacement refers to a strong price movement showing high momentum, indicated by the large-bodied candlesticks with fair value gaps in between them.

Displacement happens when price reacts aggressively to a certain price level.

You can see the example of displacement in the picture given below.

![ICT displacement example — strong impulsive bullish move with large-bodied candles and fair value gaps showing high momentum](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/ICT-Displacement-move-1.png)

For the complete study about displacement, see my dedicated [ICT Displacement Move](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-displacement-move/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Market Structure Shift (MSS)
content:
#### Market Structure Shift (MSS)

Market structure shift is the initial change in the direction of price which can lead to a reversal.

It is indicated by the break of a swing high in a bullish scenario and the break of a swing low in a bearish scenario.

You can use market structure shift as a confirmation of your trade entry.

An example of market structure shift is given below.

![ICT market structure shift example — break of a recent swing high signaling the initial bullish reversal after a bearish leg](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/ICT-Market-structure-shift-1.png)

For the complete study about ICT market structure shift, see my dedicated [ICT Market Structure Shift](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-market-structure-shift/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Break of Structure (BOS)
content:
#### Break of Structure (BOS)

Break of structure is the first major confirmation that the trend is continuing — a clean break above the previous swing high (bullish) or below the previous swing low (bearish).

BOS confirms the leg and lets you mark the inducement, the order flow and the order block inside that leg.

For the complete study, see my dedicated [Break of Structure (BOS)](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/break-of-structure-bos/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Change of Character (CHOCH)
content:
#### Change of Character (CHOCH)

Change of character is the first sign that the trend is reversing — the break of the most recent counter-trend swing point in the opposite direction.

In a bullish leg, CHOCH is the break of the most recent higher low to the downside. In a bearish leg, CHOCH is the break of the most recent lower high to the upside.

For the complete study, see my dedicated [Change of Character (CHOCH)](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/change-of-character-choch-in-trading/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Order Block
content:
#### Order Block

Order block is the area on the price chart where a cluster of buy or sell orders is placed by institutions.

An impulse price movement after the order block adds to its validity.

Bearish order block is indicated by the last bullish candlestick before an impulse bearish price move.

Bullish order block is indicated by the last bearish candlestick before an impulse bullish price move.

You can see the example of an order block in the picture given below.

![ICT order block example — last bearish candle before an impulsive bullish move marked as the bullish order block re-entry zone](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/ICT-Order-Block-1.png)

For the complete study about order blocks, see my dedicated [ICT Order Block](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-order-block/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Inducement (IDM)
content:
#### Inducement (IDM)

Inducement is a key level or market structure that persuades a FOMO retail trader to execute a trade early — a smart-money trap.

Price typically sweeps the inducement before delivering the real directional move, leaving the retail trader stopped out.

For the complete study, see my dedicated [Inducement in Forex](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/what-is-inducement-in-forex/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Daily Bias
content:
#### Daily Bias

Daily bias is the anticipated potential direction of price for the day.

Daily bias is an important ICT concept for day traders.

ICT traders use the daily chart and the lower timeframes to anticipate the price direction and then trade in that direction.

You can see the example of daily bias in the picture given below.

![ICT bearish daily bias example — daily candle aiming to take the previous day low with intraday short opportunities aligned with the bearish bias](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/ICT-bearish-daily-bias.png)

For the complete study about daily bias, see my dedicated [ICT Daily Bias](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-daily-bias-trick/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Premium and Discount Zones
content:
#### Premium and Discount Zones

Premium and discount zones are the key to trading with ICT concepts, and the Fibonacci retracement tool is used to find these zones.

Apply Fibonacci from a swing high to swing low with the inputs 0, 1 and 0.50.

The area above 0.50 is the premium zone, and the area below 0.50 is the discount zone.

The idea behind premium and discount is that a seller prefers to sell at premium and a buyer prefers to buy at discount.

You can see the example of premium and discount zones in the picture below.

![ICT premium and discount zones example — Fibonacci from swing low to swing high with the area above 50 marked as premium and the area below 50 as discount](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/ict-premium-zone.png)

For the complete study about the premium and discount zone, see my dedicated [Premium and Discount Zone](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-premium-and-discount-zone-identification/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Optimal Trade Entry (OTE)
content:
#### Optimal Trade Entry (OTE)

The Optimal Trade Entry is the 62%–79% Fibonacci retracement zone of the most recent impulsive leg — the area where smart money typically delivers the real move after sweeping the inducement.

For the complete study, see my dedicated [ICT Optimal Trade Entry](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-optimal-trade-entry/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Power of 3 (PO3 / AMD)
content:
#### Power of 3 (PO3 / AMD)

Power of 3 is the daily delivery template — Accumulation, Manipulation, Distribution. Smart money accumulates inside the Asian range, manipulates one side during London, and distributes the real move during New York.

For the complete study, see my dedicated [ICT Power of 3](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-power-of-3-po3/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Silver Bullet
content:
#### Silver Bullet

Silver Bullet is a one-hour high-probability window during the New York AM session (10:00–11:00 NY) where price typically delivers a fair value gap entry in the direction of the daily bias.

For the complete study, see my dedicated [ICT Silver Bullet](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-silver-bullet-strategy/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Killzones
content:
#### Killzones

Killzones are the specific time windows where institutional volume concentrates — Asian killzone, London killzone, New York AM killzone and New York PM killzone. Trading inside the killzones gives the highest-probability ICT setups.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: ICT Macros
content:
#### ICT Macros

ICT Macros are the 20-minute high-conviction windows inside each killzone — for example the 09:50 NY-AM macro and the 13:10 NY-PM macro — where the algorithmic delivery is most concentrated.

For the complete study, see my dedicated [ICT Macro Time-Based Strategy](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-macro-time-based-strategy/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Smart Money Reversal (SMT) Divergence
content:
#### Smart Money Reversal (SMT) Divergence

SMT divergence is the disagreement between two correlated pairs at a key liquidity level — for example EUR/USD making a higher high while GBP/USD makes a lower high. SMT confirms that smart money is rejecting the level.

For the complete study, see my dedicated [ICT SMT Divergence](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-smart-money-tool-smt-divergence/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Turtle Soup
content:
#### Turtle Soup

Turtle Soup is the failure pattern at relative equal highs or lows — price sweeps the equal level, fails to follow through, and reverses. It is one of the cleanest ICT entries against retail breakout traders.

For the complete study, see my dedicated [ICT Turtle Soup](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-turtle-soup-trading-strategy/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: Judas Swing
content:
#### Judas Swing

Judas Swing is the false move at the London open that fakes the retail trader into the wrong direction before the real London move begins. It is a manipulation phase of the daily Power of 3 template.

For the complete study, see my dedicated [ICT Judas Swing](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-judas-swing/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: IRL and ERL
content:
#### IRL and ERL

Internal Range Liquidity (IRL) is the liquidity inside a dealing range — typically the FVGs and order blocks. External Range Liquidity (ERL) is the liquidity outside the dealing range — the swing highs and lows. Price oscillates between IRL and ERL.

For the complete study, see my dedicated [IRL and ERL](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-internal-and-external-range-liquidity/>) guide.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: How to Use This List
content:
#### How to Use This List

The order in which you should learn these concepts:

  1. **Liquidity, Imbalance, Displacement** — the three forces that drive price.
  2. **BOS and CHOCH** — the structural read.
  3. **MSS** — the lower-timeframe entry trigger.
  4. **Order Block, FVG, Inducement** — the PD arrays.
  5. **Premium and Discount, OTE** — the entry refinement.
  6. **Daily Bias, Power of 3** — the directional and time framework.
  7. **Killzones, Silver Bullet, Macros, Judas Swing** — the time-based delivery windows.
  8. **SMT, Turtle Soup, IRL/ERL** — the advanced confluences.

Each concept builds on the previous one, so following the order above gives you the cleanest learning curve.

title: most-important-ict-concepts-to-conquer-market-complete-list
section: FAQs about ICT Concepts
content:
#### FAQs about ICT Concepts

Brief answers to the questions readers ask most often about the ICT concepts list.

**Who created the ICT concepts?**

Michael J. Huddleston, also known as the Inner Circle Trader. The ICT framework is built on the Interbank Price Delivery Algorithm and Smart Money Concepts.

**What are the most important ICT concepts?**

Liquidity, Imbalance (FVG), Displacement, Market Structure Shift, Order Block, Inducement, Daily Bias, Premium and Discount, OTE, Power of 3, BOS and CHOCH. These are the foundation of every ICT trade.

**In which order should I learn them?**

Liquidity, Imbalance, Displacement first — then structure (BOS, CHOCH, MSS) — then PD arrays (OB, FVG, Inducement) — then entry refinement (Premium/Discount, OTE) — then time-based delivery (Daily Bias, Power of 3, Killzones, Silver Bullet).

**Are ICT concepts the same as SMC?**

ICT and SMC overlap heavily — both are built on liquidity, imbalance and structure. SMC is essentially a derivative of ICT that some traders teach separately, but the mechanics are the same.

**Do these concepts work on indices and gold?**

Yes — ICT concepts apply cleanly to NQ, ES, XAU/USD and major forex pairs. The algorithmic delivery is consistent across asset classes.

**Where can I find the complete tutorial for each concept?**

Every section above has a link to the dedicated tutorial on this site. Click the section’s link to read the full breakdown — definition, types, identification, trade flow, common mistakes and FAQ.

**How long does it take to master ICT?**

Three to six months of focused study and chart time on a single instrument is the realistic learning curve for the core concepts. The advanced concepts (SMT, Power of 3, Macros) take longer.

**What timeframes do ICT traders use?**

Daily and 4-hour for the bias, 15-minute for the analysis, and 5-minute or 1-minute for the execution.

# MSS vs CHOCH — Smart Money Trading Differences, Bullish/Bearish Variants & Trade Flow

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/mss-vs-choch/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/mss-vs-choch/)

![MSS vs CHOCH — Market Structure Shift breaks a swing high or swing low for an initial reversal signal, while CHOCH breaks the previous market structure to confirm a long-term trend change](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/MSS-vs-CHOCH.png)

MSS vs CHOCH is one of the most common confusion points in smart money trading — both involve a structural break, both signal a shift in price delivery, but they sit at different layers of the market structure and they call for different trade decisions.

In this guide I walk you through the MSS vs CHOCH comparison — the definition of each, the bullish and bearish variants, the key differences, where each one fits in the trade flow, common mistakes and the FAQ. Real market examples are included throughout.

You can jump to the section you are most interested in from below or continue reading the full article for a complete view.

Table of Contents

[Toggle](<#>)

title: mss-vs-choch
section: What is Market Structure Shift (MSS)?
content:
#### What is Market Structure Shift (MSS)?

To understand the ICT-MSS you must know about the [ICT Swing Low](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-low-formation/>) and [ICT Swing High](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-high-explained/>).

Market Structure Shift is an ICT concept which indicates the short-term change in the delivery of price, indicated by the break of an [ICT Swing Point](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-high-explained/>).

It is the initial signal of a changing market direction, which may turn into a long-term change in the trend of price.

Most traders confuse it with the change of character (CHOCH), and that confusion may result in losing trades.

**(I) Bullish Market Structure Shift** happens when price breaks a [Swing High Point](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-high-explained/>). It indicates that price delivery for the short term has changed to buy-side.

![Bullish ICT Market Structure Shift example — price breaks the most recent swing high signaling the initial bullish shift in short-term delivery](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/ict-Market-sTRUCTUREsHIFT.png)

This may be due to price going to take inducement or to reach a higher-timeframe [PD Array](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-pd-array-key-to-trade-execution/>), and it may result in a Change of Character as well.

**(II) Bearish Market Structure Shift** happens when price breaks a [Swing Low Point](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-low-formation/>). It indicates that price delivery for the short term has changed to sell-side.

![Bearish ICT Market Structure Shift example — price breaks the most recent swing low signaling the initial bearish shift in short-term delivery](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/ICT-MSS.png)

This may be due to price going to take inducement or to reach a higher-timeframe [PD Array](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-pd-array-key-to-trade-execution/>), and it may result in a Change of Character as well.

title: mss-vs-choch
section: What is Change of Character (CHOCH)?
content:
#### What is Change of Character (CHOCH)?

To understand the Change of Character (CHOCH) you must know about market structure and the valid highs and lows of price, for which I will refer you to my [CHOCH guide](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/change-of-character-choch-in-trading/>).

Change of Character (CHOCH) is a smart money concept which indicates the long-term change in the delivery of price — the change of market trend itself.

It is indicated by the break of previous market structure in the opposite direction — bullish to bearish or bearish to bullish.

![ICT CHOCH example — break of the previous higher low after a bullish leg, signaling the long-term change of character from bullish to bearish](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/choch.png)

**(I) In a bullish market structure** , Change of Character (CHOCH) is indicated by the break of the previous higher low resulting in a new lower low.

It indicates that the trend of price has changed from bullish to bearish.

**(II) In a bearish market structure** , Change of Character (CHOCH) is indicated by the break of the previous lower high resulting in a new higher high.

It indicates that the trend of price has changed from bearish to bullish.

title: mss-vs-choch
section: MSS vs CHOCH — The Key Differences
content:
#### MSS vs CHOCH — The Key Differences

Both MSS and CHOCH involve a structural break, but they sit at different layers and tell you different things.

**(1) The level that gets broken.** MSS breaks a swing high or swing low — a recent intraday extreme. CHOCH breaks the most recent higher low (in a bullish trend) or lower high (in a bearish trend) — a structural extreme.

**(2) The signal strength.** MSS is the INITIAL signal that delivery has shifted in the short term. CHOCH is the CONFIRMATION that the long-term trend has changed.

**(3) The order of appearance.** MSS often comes first inside a leg. CHOCH typically requires the MSS to be followed by additional structure that breaks the higher low or lower high.

**(4) The trade decision.** MSS is used as the lower-timeframe entry trigger inside a higher-timeframe PD array. CHOCH is used as the higher-timeframe bias flip — the moment to start looking for setups in the new direction.

**(5) The reliability.** MSS can fail and resolve back into the prior trend. CHOCH has a higher base rate of marking a real trend change because it requires the structural extreme to break.

title: mss-vs-choch
section: Where Each One Fits in the Trade Flow
content:
#### Where Each One Fits in the Trade Flow

I use both MSS and CHOCH together — they are not competing concepts, they are different layers of the same structure.

**Higher-timeframe CHOCH** tells me the bias has flipped — bullish to bearish or vice versa.

**Higher-timeframe BOS** tells me the existing bias is continuing.

**Lower-timeframe MSS** tells me the entry trigger has fired inside a higher-timeframe PD array.

In practice — wait for the higher-timeframe CHOCH or BOS, identify the higher-timeframe PD array, drop to the lower timeframe, wait for the MSS at the PD array, then enter on the MSS retest.

title: mss-vs-choch
section: Step-by-Step Trade Flow Using MSS and CHOCH
content:
#### Step-by-Step Trade Flow Using MSS and CHOCH

This is the exact sequence I run when using both concepts together.

  1. **Set the higher-timeframe bias.** 1-day and 4-hour structure — has there been a recent CHOCH? If yes, the bias has flipped. If no, the existing trend is intact.
  2. **Mark the higher-timeframe PD array.** Order block, FVG or breaker that price is drawn to inside the bias-aligned zone.
  3. **Wait for price to reach the PD array.** Confirmation that the algorithm is delivering toward the level.
  4. **Drop to the lower timeframe (5-minute or 15-minute).** For the MSS read.
  5. **Wait for the lower-timeframe MSS.** A clean break of the most recent counter-trend swing point in the bias direction.
  6. **Mark the post-MSS PD array.** The fair value gap or order block left behind by the displacement after the MSS.
  7. **Enter on the retest of the post-MSS PD array.** In the higher-timeframe direction.
  8. **Set the stop.** Above or below the MSS swing high or low (depending on direction).
  9. **Take profit at the next draw on liquidity.** Old high or low, relative equal level, or higher-timeframe FVG.

title: mss-vs-choch
section: Does CHOCH Always Result in a Change of Trend?
content:
#### Does CHOCH Always Result in a Change of Trend?

Trading is the game of probabilities — nothing is certain here. Every concept including CHOCH gives a high probability of happening, but it may fail too.

That does not hurt — because the success ratio of CHOCH is greater than its failure ratio, and at the end it results in profits.

When CHOCH does fail, it usually fails by being a deep retracement that gets reclaimed before the structural extreme. The fix is to wait for the post-CHOCH MSS retest before committing — that lets the failed CHOCHs filter themselves out before you enter.

title: mss-vs-choch
section: Best Pairs for Trading MSS and CHOCH
content:
#### Best Pairs for Trading MSS and CHOCH

Both MSS and CHOCH work on every major pair — GBP/USD, EUR/USD, USD/CAD, plus metals such as XAU/USD and XAG/USD. The cleanest prints come from instruments that produce strong displacement legs.

**For traders in the United States** who follow the CFTC FIFO and no-hedge rules, both frameworks map cleanly onto NQ and ES futures (CME Group) plus regulated forex pairs through US-based brokers. The 09:50 NY-AM [macro window](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-macro-time-based-strategy/>) is a particularly strong place to watch for MSS triggers because the algorithmic delivery is most concentrated there.

title: mss-vs-choch
section: Common Mistakes Around MSS and CHOCH
content:
#### Common Mistakes Around MSS and CHOCH

These are the recurring mistakes I see when traders first start working with both concepts.

  1. **Trading the MSS as if it were a CHOCH.** MSS is a short-term shift. Treating it as a full trend reversal flips the bias too early and produces counter-trend trades.
  2. **Waiting for CHOCH before entering on every trade.** CHOCH is the bias flip — not the entry. The entry is the lower-timeframe MSS at a bias-aligned PD array.
  3. **Confusing MSS with BOS.** MSS breaks a swing high or low. BOS breaks the previous structure AFTER taking inducement. See my [BOS guide](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/break-of-structure-bos/>) for the BOS-vs-MSS comparison.
  4. **Treating every wick as a structural break.** Both MSS and CHOCH require a candle to close beyond the structure — a wick alone is a stop hunt, not a confirmed break.
  5. **Skipping the higher-timeframe context.** An MSS aligned with the higher-timeframe trend is a high-probability trigger. An MSS against the higher-timeframe trend is unreliable.
  6. **Treating CHOCH and MSS as competing concepts.** They are different layers of the same structure. Use CHOCH for the bias and MSS for the trigger — not one or the other.

title: mss-vs-choch
section: FAQs about MSS vs CHOCH
content:
#### FAQs about MSS vs CHOCH

Brief answers to the questions readers ask most often about MSS vs CHOCH.

**What is the difference between MSS and CHOCH?**

MSS breaks a swing high or swing low — short-term delivery shift. CHOCH breaks the most recent higher low (bullish trend) or lower high (bearish trend) — long-term trend change. MSS is the initial signal; CHOCH is the confirmation.

**Is MSS the same as BOS?**

No. MSS breaks a swing point. BOS breaks the previous structure AFTER taking inducement. MSS is the initial reversal signal; BOS is the continuation confirmation.

**Can MSS happen without CHOCH?**

Yes — MSS can happen and resolve back into the prior trend without ever producing a CHOCH. That is exactly when MSS becomes a stop-hunt trap rather than a real reversal.

**Can CHOCH happen without MSS?**

In practice no — CHOCH typically follows an MSS by definition, because the move that breaks the higher low or lower high will first break a swing point along the way.

**Which one do I trade — MSS or CHOCH?**

Both, but for different reasons. Use CHOCH to set the higher-timeframe bias. Use MSS as the lower-timeframe entry trigger inside a bias-aligned PD array.

**Where do I place the stop loss when trading the MSS?**

Above the MSS swing high (for sell trades) or below the MSS swing low (for buy trades), with a small buffer.

**What timeframe is best for spotting MSS?**

5-minute and 15-minute for the MSS trigger. 1-day and 4-hour for the CHOCH-based bias.

**Does CHOCH always result in a change of trend?**

No — trading is the game of probabilities. CHOCH gives a high probability of trend change but may fail. Its success ratio is greater than its failure ratio.

**What if MSS fires but CHOCH never confirms?**

Then the move was a short-term shift that did not reach the structural extreme. The original trend is still in place, and the next setup should align with it.

**Do MSS and CHOCH work on indices and gold?**

Yes — NQ, ES and XAU/USD all produce textbook MSS and CHOCH prints, especially during the New York AM session and around US economic releases.

**How does CHOCH relate to BOS?**

CHOCH and BOS are opposites in direction. CHOCH = trend reversal. BOS = trend continuation. In a bullish leg, CHOCH is the break of the most recent higher low; BOS is the break of the most recent higher high.

# Pin Bar Trading Strategy — Bullish/Bearish Reversal at S&R with ICT Mapping

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/pin-bar-trading-strategy/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/pin-bar-trading-strategy/)

![Pin Bar Trading Strategy — single-candlestick rejection pattern with long wick and small body at support and resistance for bullish and bearish reversal trades](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/PIN-BAR-TRADING-STRATEGY.png)

Pin Bar Trading Strategy is one of the cleanest single-candle reversal signals in price action — a long rejection wick combined with a small body shows that price tried to move past a key level and was forcibly rejected back, signaling that the level has held and a reversal is likely. Mastering pin bar entry at strong support and resistance is one of the highest hit-rate price-action setups in technical trading.

A pin bar pattern consists of a single candlestick price bar that represents a sharp reversal and rejection of price from a key level (support or resistance).

Before going in-depth on pin bar trading strategy, you should learn about [Support and Resistance](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/support-resistance-trading/>) — because a pin bar is mostly reliable at strong support or resistance levels.

In this guide I walk you through the pin bar concept — the candlestick definition, the bullish and bearish variants, the trade execution at support and resistance, the step-by-step trade flow, common mistakes and the FAQ.

You can jump to the section you are most interested in from below or continue reading the full article for a complete view.
