# Inducement in Forex / ICT Inducement (IDM) — Smart Money Trap Identification & Avoidance

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/what-is-inducement-in-forex/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/what-is-inducement-in-forex/)

![Inducement in forex / ICT Inducement \(IDM\) — smart money trap that lures FOMO traders into early entries before price reverses](https://www.innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/inducement-in-forex-2.png)

Inducement trading involves identifying and avoiding the smart-money traps used to manipulate retail traders into executing sell or buy orders early.

Inducement in forex (also called ICT Inducement or IDM in trading) is an area on the price chart that triggers FOMO traders to execute trades early — and that early entry results in a loss when price sweeps the inducement before continuing the real move.

To be a successful trader you should know about these smart-money traps and avoid them.

In this guide I walk you through the inducement concept — the meaning, the BOS and CHOCH variants, the avoidance rule, the step-by-step trade flow, common mistakes and the FAQ. Real market examples are included throughout.

You can jump to the section you are most interested in from below or continue reading the full article for a complete view.

Table of Contents

title: what-is-inducement-in-forex
section: What is Inducement in Trading?
content:
#### What is Inducement in Trading?

The act of persuading someone to do something is called inducement. In trading, inducement means any key level or market structure that persuades a FOMO trader to execute a trade.

It is a smart-money trap for retail traders, which leads them to believe in a certain bullish or bearish move.

In reality price does not move that way — it goes against the retail trader’s expectations, sweeping the inducement before delivering the real direction.

You can see the example of inducement trading in the illustration below.

![Inducement in forex example — smart money sweeps the FOMO retail trader's stop above the inducement level before the real bearish move](https://www.innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/inducement-in-forex-1.png)

title: what-is-inducement-in-forex
section: What Does IDM Mean in Trading?
content:
#### What Does IDM Mean in Trading?

IDM is the abbreviation of “Inducement”. It is the same concept used by SMC and ICT traders interchangeably — when you see “IDM in trading” or “inducement in SMC”, both refer to the same retail-trap level that price has to sweep before the algorithm delivers the real direction.

title: what-is-inducement-in-forex
section: How to Identify Inducement in Forex
content:
#### How to Identify Inducement in Forex

As discussed, inducement is a smart-money trap which can take the form of an [order block](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-order-block/>), a [supply & demand zone](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/supply-and-demand-in-forex-trading/>) or a [support & resistance area](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/support-resistance-trading/>).

The challenge is to identify which order block, supply/demand zone or support/resistance zone is inducement, and which is a valid point of interest for executing a trade.

To identify inducement in the forex market you should first know about [valid pullback](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/3-step-guide-to-master-valid-pullback/>), [break of structure (BOS)](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/break-of-structure-bos/>) and [change of character (CHOCH)](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/change-of-character-choch-in-trading/>).

After going through these SMC concepts you will be able to understand valid inducement very well.

title: what-is-inducement-in-forex
section: Types of Inducement in Trading
content:
#### Types of Inducement in Trading

For better understanding, inducement is divided into two major types.

title: what-is-inducement-in-forex
section: Inducement in Case of CHOCH
content:
#### Inducement in Case of CHOCH

In the case of a CHOCH, the inducement is the very first pullback before price changed its character.

In other words: when price changes its character you have to look back into the price leg that led to the CHOCH and find a valid pullback. That pullback is the inducement.

Real market examples of inducement in the case of bullish and bearish CHOCH are shown below.

![Bullish CHOCH inducement example — first pullback before the change of character marked as the inducement level that price must sweep before reversing](https://www.innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/inducement-in-forex.png)

![Bearish CHOCH inducement example — first pullback in the bearish leg marked as the inducement that traps early sellers](https://www.innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/inducement-in-trading.png)

title: what-is-inducement-in-forex
section: Inducement in Case of BOS
content:
#### Inducement in Case of BOS

Inducement in the case of BOS is the very first pullback before the market broke the structure.

In other words: when price breaks its structure you have to look back into the price leg that led to the BOS and find a valid pullback. That pullback is the inducement.

Real market examples of inducement in the case of bullish and bearish BOS are shown below.

![Bullish BOS inducement example — first pullback in the leg that broke the prior swing high marked as inducement](https://www.innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/inducement.png)

![Bearish BOS inducement example — first pullback in the leg that broke the prior swing low marked as inducement](https://www.innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/inducement-forex.png)

title: what-is-inducement-in-forex
section: Inducement After Break of Structure
content:
#### Inducement After Break of Structure

After a major BOS, price may shift its high without breaking the structure. In this scenario, mark the price leg that broke the high and find the valid pullback inside it. The valid pullback before breaking the high becomes the valid inducement.

For the detailed study see my dedicated [Inducement After Break of Structure](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/inducement-after-break-of-structure/>) guide.

title: what-is-inducement-in-forex
section: How to Avoid Inducement in Forex
content:
#### How to Avoid Inducement in Forex

To avoid inducement in forex, follow just one rule: **“Do not take a trade until the inducement is grabbed.”**

In a bullish trend you should not take a buy trade until price clears the inducement by going below the inducement low and hunting the stop losses.

In a bearish trend you should not take a sell trade until price goes up and clears the inducement by going above the inducement high.

title: what-is-inducement-in-forex
section: Step-by-Step Inducement Trade Flow
content:
#### Step-by-Step Inducement Trade Flow

This is the exact sequence I run when trading around an inducement level.

  1. **Read the higher-timeframe context.** 1-day and 4-hour charts — bullish, bearish or neutral structure.
  2. **Identify a CHOCH or BOS.** A change of character or a break of structure on the analysis timeframe.
  3. **Look back into the leg that produced it.** Find the first valid pullback inside the impulse leg that led to the CHOCH/BOS.
  4. **Mark the inducement level.** The high or low of that first pullback. This is the inducement that retail traders are using as a buy/sell zone.
  5. **Wait for the sweep.** Bullish trend — price must dip below the inducement low. Bearish trend — price must spike above the inducement high.
  6. **Wait for confirmation.** A lower-timeframe MSS, a fair value gap or an order block formed after the sweep.
  7. **Enter on the retest.** Take the trade in the higher-timeframe direction at the post-sweep PD array.
  8. **Set the stop.** Beyond the swept inducement extreme, with a small buffer.
  9. **Take profit at the next draw on liquidity.** Old high/low, relative equal level or higher-timeframe FVG.

title: what-is-inducement-in-forex
section: Best Timeframe for Inducement Trading
content:
#### Best Timeframe for Inducement Trading

To mark the inducement and execute a trade on the basis of inducement, use the 15-minute timeframe.

But you should always have a clear idea of the higher-timeframe market structure using the 1-day and 4-hour charts. Without higher-timeframe context, every pullback looks like an inducement and the avoidance rule becomes ineffective.

title: what-is-inducement-in-forex
section: Best Pairs for Inducement Trading
content:
#### Best Pairs for Inducement Trading

Inducement trading works best on almost all trading pairs — currencies like GBP/USD, EUR/USD or USD/CAD, plus metals such as XAU/USD or XAG/USD.

XTI/USD (also known as USOIL) is harder to tackle using this strategy and has a lower win rate because the oil market produces more false sweeps that do not lead to a clean directional follow-through.

**For traders in the United States** who follow the CFTC FIFO and no-hedge rules, the inducement framework maps cleanly onto NQ and ES futures (CME Group) plus regulated forex pairs through US-based brokers. The 09:50 NY-AM [macro window](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-macro-time-based-strategy/>) is a particularly strong place to watch for inducement sweeps because the algorithmic delivery is concentrated there.

title: what-is-inducement-in-forex
section: Common Mistakes Around Inducement
content:
#### Common Mistakes Around Inducement

These are the recurring mistakes I see when traders first start trading the inducement concept.

  1. **Entering before the inducement is swept.** The avoidance rule exists for a reason. Pre-positioning into the inducement zone almost always ends with a stopped trade as price sweeps the level.
  2. **Marking every pullback as inducement.** Only the FIRST valid pullback inside the leg that produced the BOS or CHOCH qualifies. Marking every pullback turns the chart into noise.
  3. **No higher-timeframe bias.** Inducement avoidance only matters when you have a directional thesis. In a choppy range, every level looks like an inducement and the framework collapses.
  4. **Confusing inducement with the entry zone.** Inducement is the level you wait for price to SWEEP. The entry zone is the PD array (FVG, order block) that forms AFTER the sweep — not the inducement itself.
  5. **Stop too tight after the sweep.** The stop must sit beyond the swept inducement extreme — not at the inducement level itself. Tight stops parked at the inducement get hunted on the second test.
  6. **Trading every CHOCH/BOS without inducement context.** A BOS or CHOCH without a clear inducement to sweep is a less reliable setup. The inducement-then-reverse pattern is the high-conviction variant.

title: what-is-inducement-in-forex
section: FAQs about Inducement in Forex
content:
#### FAQs about Inducement in Forex

Brief answers to the questions readers ask most often about inducement.

**What is inducement in trading?**

Inducement is a key level or market structure that persuades a FOMO retail trader to execute a trade early. It is a smart-money trap — price typically sweeps the inducement before delivering the real directional move, leaving the retail trader stopped out.

**What is the difference between inducement in ICT and inducement in SMC?**

There is no functional difference. ICT and SMC traders use the same concept — a retail-trap level that price must sweep before the real move. SMC traders sometimes call it “IDM”; ICT traders use “inducement”. The mechanic is identical.

**What does IDM mean in trading?**

IDM is the abbreviation of Inducement. The two terms are interchangeable in modern smart-money concepts material.

**What are the two types of inducement?**

(1) Inducement in case of CHOCH — the very first pullback before price changed its character. (2) Inducement in case of BOS — the very first pullback before the market broke the structure. Both are valid retail traps that smart money sweeps before delivering the real direction.

**How do I avoid inducement in forex?**

Follow one rule: “Do not take a trade until the inducement is grabbed.” In a bullish trend, wait for price to dip below the inducement low. In a bearish trend, wait for price to spike above the inducement high. Only then look for the entry.

**Where do I enter after the inducement is swept?**

After the sweep, wait for a lower-timeframe Market Structure Shift, a fair value gap or an order block to form. Enter on the retest of that PD array — not on the inducement itself.

**Where is the stop loss?**

Beyond the swept inducement extreme — below the inducement low for buy trades, above the inducement high for sell trades, with a small buffer.

**What timeframe is best for inducement trading?**

Use the 15-minute for marking and execution. Use the 1-day and 4-hour for the higher-timeframe market structure context.

**Which pairs work best with inducement trading?**

GBP/USD, EUR/USD, USD/CAD, XAU/USD and XAG/USD. XTI/USD (oil) has a lower win rate and is harder to read.

**What is inducement after break of structure?**

After a major BOS, price may shift its high without breaking the structure again. The valid pullback in the leg that broke the prior high becomes the valid inducement. See the dedicated [Inducement After Break of Structure](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/inducement-after-break-of-structure/>) guide for the deep dive.

**Is inducement the same as a liquidity sweep?**

Inducement is the level. The liquidity sweep is the action of price taking that level. Closely related concepts — the inducement is what gets swept, and the sweep is what creates the entry opportunity afterward.

**Does inducement work on indices and gold?**

Yes — NQ, ES and XAU/USD all produce textbook inducement-and-sweep patterns, especially during the New York AM session and around US economic releases.

# ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 3 Notes — NDOG, NWOG & PM Session Trading + Free PDF

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-2024/ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-3/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-2024/ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-3/)

![ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 3 — notes on the New Day Opening Gap \(NDOG\), New Week Opening Gap \(NWOG\) and the post-NY-lunch afternoon-session model](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ICT-2024-Mentorship-Lecture-3.png)

In this third lecture of the ICT 2024 Mentorship Program, we look into the characteristics of the ICT New Day Opening Gap (NDOG) and the New Week Opening Gap (NWOG).

These gaps often act as powerful magnets for price action, either serving as a draw-on-liquidity or aligning with a PD array.

Understanding how these gaps influence market behaviour is crucial for traders aiming to refine their strategies.

This session specifically emphasises the significance of observing market movements during the afternoon and post-New York lunch hour — periods when these gaps often play a pivotal role in price dynamics.

Below are my full Lecture 3 notes — the key elements, the key timeframes, the AM and PM-session models, the OTE setup after lunch and the free PDF download.

Table of Contents

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-3
section: Lecture 3 Quick Summary
content:
#### Lecture 3 Quick Summary

ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 3 introduces the NDOG and NWOG as the strongest inefficiencies on the chart — stronger than relative equal highs and lows. Keep at least four NDOGs annotated. Trade the AM-session at 07:00 AM, 08:00 AM and 09:00 AM (NY local) when price approaches an NDOG. If there is no market-driver news in the morning, expect a rangy day with false break-outs and trade after the New York lunch hour — between 01:30 PM and 02:30 PM NY local — when an OTE setup typically prints.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-3
section: Key Elements (Definitions)
content:
#### Key Elements (Definitions)

**(I) New Day Opening Gap :** abbreviated as [NDOG](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-new-day-opening-gap-ndog/>) — it is the gap between the closing price at 05:00 PM (New York local time) and the opening price at 06:00 PM (New York local time).

**(II) New Week Opening Gap :** abbreviated as [NWOG](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-new-week-opening-gap-nwog/>) — it is the gap between the closing price on Friday at 05:00 PM (New York local time) and the opening price on Monday at 06:00 PM (New York local time).

**(III)[Market Structure Shift](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-market-structure-shift/>) :** is the initial change in the delivery of price which indicates a short-term change in trend.

**(IV)[Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/fair-value-gap-trading-strategy/>) :** is a three-candle formation having a gap between the 1st and 3rd candle’s wicks.

**(V)[Inverse Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-inversion-fair-value-gap/>) :** is a failed fair value gap which works inversely.

**(VI)[Breaker Block](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-breaker-block-trading/>) :** is a failed order block.

**(VII)[Liquidity Sweep](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-liquidity-sweep-vs-liquidity-run/>) :** is the phenomenon of hunting liquidity above highs and below lows.

**(VIII) Relative Equal Highs :** is when a high has a lower swing high on the right side of it formed due to price swing failure.

**(IX) Relative Equal Lows :** is when a swing low has a higher swing low on the right side of it formed due to price swing failure.

**(X)[Consequent Encroachment](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-consequent-encroachment/>) :** is the 50% retracement level of a PD array.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-3
section: Key Times of the Day
content:
#### Key Times of the Day

**(I)** 07:00 AM, 08:00 AM and 09:00 AM (the AM-session)

**(II)** Afternoon session (post 12:00 PM NY local time)

**(III)** After New York lunch hour (01:30 PM NY local time)

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-3
section: Application in the Market
content:
#### Application in the Market

New Day Opening Gaps and New Week Opening Gaps are the strongest inefficiencies and draw-on-liquidity levels — stronger than relative equal highs and lows.

You need to have at least four NDOGs on your chart and they act as a magnet for price by drawing price to themselves.

An NDOG can tell you where price is likely to draw even before the formation of relative equal highs and lows, and you can even predict relative equal highs/lows by using these gaps.

The morning session demands more expertise and the afternoon session is relatively easier. If there is no market-driver news in the AM-session, expect a rangy day with false breakouts and price trading back to range.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-3
section: (I) Bearish Bias
content:
#### (I) Bearish Bias

If you have a single or multiple New Day Opening Gaps above price and your [bias](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-daily-bias-explained/>) is bearish, then wait for price to get to those NDOGs at 07:00 AM, 08:00 AM or 09:00 AM (New York local time).

When price approaches these NDOGs, look for an ICT MSS to the sell side. After the MSS, when price retraces back, look for a sell trade at the breaker block or the IFVG.

Your stop loss in this case will be above the high formed post-07:00 AM liquidity hunt. For take profit you can target the next draw-on-liquidity, such as relative equal lows or the previous session low.

If the New Day Opening Gap is below price and your bias is bearish, then this NDOG will act as the draw-on-liquidity and price will draw toward it.

![ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 3 bearish setup — NDOG above price acts as the draw, MSS to the sell side after the 07:00 AM tap and short entry at the breaker or IFVG](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ict-2024-mentorshiplecture-3-1.png)

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-3
section: (II) Bullish Bias
content:
#### (II) Bullish Bias

If you have a single or multiple New Day Opening Gaps below price and your [bias](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-daily-bias-explained/>) is bullish, then wait for price to get to those NDOGs at 07:00 AM, 08:00 AM or 09:00 AM (New York local time).

When price approaches these NDOGs, look for an ICT MSS to the buy side. After the MSS, when price retraces back, look for a buy trade at the breaker block or the IFVG.

Your stop loss in this case will be below the low formed post-07:00 AM liquidity hunt. For take profit you can target the next draw-on-liquidity, such as relative equal highs or the previous session high.

If the New Day Opening Gap is above price and your bias is bullish, then this NDOG will act as the draw-on-liquidity and price will draw toward it.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-3
section: Note — When Morning is Quiet, Trade the Afternoon
content:
#### Note — When Morning is Quiet, Trade the Afternoon

If there is no market-driver news in the morning then look for the trading opportunity in the afternoon session — preferably after the New York lunch hour at 01:30 PM (New York local time).

Between 01:30 PM and 02:30 PM (NY local time) you can get an [ICT Optimal Trade Entry](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-optimal-trade-entry-ote-pattern/>).

![ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 3 afternoon-session OTE setup — between 01:30 PM and 02:30 PM NY local time, after the lunch hour](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ict-2024-mentorshiplecture-3-OTE.png)

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-3
section: Step-by-Step Lecture 3 Trade Flow
content:
#### Step-by-Step Lecture 3 Trade Flow

This is the exact sequence Michael Huddleston walks through in Lecture 3, condensed into a checklist.

  1. **Annotate at least four NDOGs.** Mark the 05:00 PM close to 06:00 PM open gap on the daily chart for the last four sessions.
  2. **Annotate the active NWOG.** Friday 05:00 PM close to Monday 06:00 PM open.
  3. **Set the daily bias.** Bullish, bearish or neutral on the daily and H4.
  4. **Identify the relevant NDOG for the day.** NDOGs above price are draws-on-liquidity in a bearish bias; NDOGs below price are draws in a bullish bias.
  5. **Wait for the AM-session tap.** Price must approach the NDOG at 07:00 AM, 08:00 AM or 09:00 AM NY local time.
  6. **Wait for the MSS.** A clean Market Structure Shift in the direction of the bias confirms intent.
  7. **Mark the IFVG and breaker.** The Inverse Fair Value Gap and the breaker block formed after the MSS become the entry zones.
  8. **Enter on the retracement.** Take the trade at the breaker block or the IFVG (the original lecture lists IFVG and breaker block — pick the one closest to the MSS).
  9. **Set the stop.** Above the high formed post-07:00 AM liquidity hunt (shorts) or below the low formed post-07:00 AM liquidity hunt (longs).
  10. **Take profit at the next draw on liquidity.** Relative equal levels or prior session high/low.
  11. **If the AM is quiet, switch to PM.** Look for the OTE setup between 01:30 PM and 02:30 PM NY local time.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-3
section: Best Markets for the Lecture 3 Model
content:
#### Best Markets for the Lecture 3 Model

The model is built around the New York open and afternoon, so it works best on instruments active during those windows.

  * **NQ (NASDAQ futures)** and **ES (S &P 500 futures)** — daily NDOGs are highly visible on US index charts and the AM/PM session structure is the most natural fit.
  * **GBP/USD** and **EUR/USD** — the AM-session NDOG sweep often provides the cleanest forex setup of the day.
  * **XAU/USD (Gold)** — afternoon-session OTE setups around 01:30 to 02:30 PM ET deliver clean reactions, especially on news-driven days.

**For traders in the United States** who follow the CFTC FIFO and no-hedge rules, NQ and ES on the 1-minute chart are the most natural fit for the Lecture 3 NDOG model. The post-lunch OTE window from 01:30 to 02:30 PM ET aligns directly with the NYSE-open afternoon flow on US futures and CME Group instruments.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-3
section: Common Mistakes on the Lecture 3 Model
content:
#### Common Mistakes on the Lecture 3 Model

These are the recurring mistakes I see when traders first try to apply the Lecture 3 framework.

  1. **Annotating only one NDOG.** Lecture 3 explicitly calls for at least four NDOGs on the chart. Older NDOGs continue to react.
  2. **Wrong NDOG-to-bias pairing.** NDOGs above price draw bearish setups; NDOGs below price draw bullish setups. Reversing the pairing inverts the entire trade.
  3. **Forcing AM trades on a quiet morning.** If there is no market-driver news in the morning, the lecture explicitly tells you to wait for the afternoon. Trading a rangy AM produces chop entries.
  4. **Skipping the MSS.** Without the lower-timeframe Market Structure Shift, the NDOG tap is just a wick — not a tradeable reversal.
  5. **Stop too tight.** The stop must sit beyond the entire post-07:00 AM swing — not just at the MSS pivot.
  6. **Missing the 01:30 PM window.** The OTE setup between 01:30 and 02:30 PM is one of the most reliable in the framework. Ignoring it means missing the best second-chance entry of the day.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-3
section: FAQs about ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 3
content:
#### FAQs about ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 3

Brief answers to the questions readers ask most often about Lecture 3.

**What does ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 3 cover?**

Lecture 3 introduces the New Day Opening Gap (NDOG) and the New Week Opening Gap (NWOG) as the strongest inefficiencies on the chart, walks through the AM-session model at 07:00 AM, 08:00 AM and 09:00 AM, and covers the post-lunch OTE setup between 01:30 PM and 02:30 PM NY local time.

**What is an NDOG?**

NDOG stands for New Day Opening Gap — the gap between the closing price at 05:00 PM and the opening price at 06:00 PM, both in New York local time.

**What is an NWOG according to Lecture 3?**

NWOG stands for New Week Opening Gap — Lecture 3 defines it as the gap between the closing price on Friday at 05:00 PM and the opening price on Monday at 06:00 PM, both in New York local time.

**How many NDOGs should I annotate?**

Lecture 3 calls for at least four NDOGs on the chart at all times. Older NDOGs continue to react when price returns to them.

**How do I trade a bearish NDOG setup?**

With a bearish bias and the NDOG above price, wait for price to tap the NDOG at 07:00, 08:00 or 09:00 AM NY local. Wait for an MSS to the sell side, then enter on a retest of the breaker block or the IFVG. Stop above the post-07:00 AM swing high; target the next draw-on-liquidity.

**How do I trade a bullish NDOG setup?**

With a bullish bias and the NDOG below price, wait for price to tap the NDOG at 07:00, 08:00 or 09:00 AM NY local. Wait for an MSS to the buy side, then enter on a retest of the breaker block or the IFVG. Stop below the post-07:00 AM swing low; target the next draw-on-liquidity.

**What is the post-lunch OTE setup?**

If the morning is quiet (no market-driver news), the lecture instructs traders to wait for the afternoon session. Between 01:30 PM and 02:30 PM NY local time an Optimal Trade Entry typically prints — that is the second-chance setup for the day.

**What if the NDOG is below price and bias is bearish?**

The NDOG below price acts as a draw-on-liquidity in a bearish bias — price will draw toward it. The trade plan is then to wait for price to reach the NDOG before considering a new entry on the next day’s tap.

**Can I download Lecture 3 as a PDF?**

Yes — the free PDF download button is available on the page. The PDF is sponsored by ICTPDF.COM.

**What is the difference between NDOG and NWOG?**

NDOG is the daily gap (05:00 PM close to 06:00 PM open). NWOG is the weekly gap (Friday 05:00 PM close to Monday 06:00 PM open per Lecture 3). Both act as magnets for price, but the NWOG is the higher-tier reference.

# ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 4 Notes — 08:30 AM News & 09:30 AM Open Model + Free PDF

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-2024/ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-4/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-2024/ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-4/)

Welcome to the fourth lecture notes of the ICT 2024 Mentorship series. In this lecture, Michael provides a detailed analysis of key market drivers and their implications for trading strategies.

He emphasises the importance of market-driver news released at 08:30, which can significantly influence market movements.

Michael also explores the strategic relevance of the new day and new week opening gaps, highlighting how these gaps can signal market inefficiency and liquidity.

He discusses the impact of the 09:30 market open, illustrating how this critical moment can create trading opportunities.

This lecture offers essential insights for traders looking to refine their strategies and better navigate the complexities of the market.

Below are my full Lecture 4 notes — the key elements, the key timeframes, the bullish and bearish news-day models, the 09:30 AM A-plus setup and the free PDF download.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-4
section: Lecture 4 Quick Summary
content:
#### Lecture 4 Quick Summary

ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 4 is the news-day model. The trader is at the screen by 08:30 AM (news release) and by 09:30 AM (equity market open). The framework uses NDOGs and NWOGs as the cluster of inefficiency that price draws toward, and the trade is taken from a 1-minute MSS at the breaker block or fair value gap. The 09:30 AM equity-market open often delivers the “A-plus” setup if price is still spooling toward the gap cluster after the 08:30 release. The Quarters of a Gap (0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1) are introduced as the key Fibonacci references for measuring partial-fill behaviour.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-4
section: Key Elements (Definitions)
content:
#### Key Elements (Definitions)

**(I) New Day Opening Gap :** abbreviated as [NDOG](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-new-day-opening-gap-ndog/>) — it is the gap between the closing price at 05:00 PM (NY local time) and the opening price at 06:00 PM (NY local time).

**(II) New Week Opening Gap :** abbreviated as [NWOG](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-new-week-opening-gap-nwog/>) — it is the gap between the closing price on Friday at 05:00 PM (NY local time) and the opening price on Monday at 06:00 PM (NY local time).

**(III)[Market Structure Shift](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-market-structure-shift/>) :** is the initial change in the delivery of price which indicates a short-term change in trend.

**(IV)[Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/fair-value-gap-trading-strategy/>) :** is a three-candle formation having a gap between the 1st and 3rd candle’s wicks.

**(V)[Inverse Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-inversion-fair-value-gap/>) :** is a failed fair value gap which works inversely.

**(VI)[Breaker Block](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-breaker-block-trading/>) :** is a failed order block.

**(VII)[Liquidity Sweep](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-liquidity-sweep-vs-liquidity-run/>) :** is the phenomenon of hunting liquidity above highs and below lows.

**(VIII) Relative Equal Highs :** is when a high has a lower swing high on the right side of it formed due to price swing failure.

**(IX) Relative Equal Lows :** is when a swing low has a higher swing low on the right side of it formed due to price swing failure.

**(X)[Consequent Encroachment](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-consequent-encroachment/>) :** is the 50% retracement level of a PD array.

**(XI) Quarters of a Gap :** use the following Fibonacci settings to find the quarter levels of a New Day Opening Gap or a New Week Opening Gap — 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.

**(XII)[Premium and Discount](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-premium-and-discount-zone-identification/>) :** the premium zone is above the 50% retracement level between an established high and low, while the discount zone is below the 50% retracement.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-4
section: Application in the Market
content:
#### Application in the Market

Lecture 4 of the ICT 2024 mentorship is built on the economic news at 08:30 AM. ICT suggests not focusing on the numbers or the news headline because the charts tell the real story.

You will use the New Day Opening Gap and the New Week Opening Gap as inefficiencies and the draw-on-liquidity.

News will draw price to the cluster of these inefficiencies, and the real move comes after 09:30 AM because of the actual market opening.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-4
section: (I) Bearish Bias
content:
#### (I) Bearish Bias

If your [daily bias](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-daily-bias-explained/>) is bearish on the news day, you look for New Day Opening Gaps and New Week Opening Gaps above price in the [premium](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-premium-and-discount-zone-identification/>) zone. If there is no gap, you can look for a Fair Value Gap or an Inversion Fair Value Gap.

Most often, before the news at 08:30 AM, price looks sandwiched between two levels that could be a gap.

At 08:30 AM, after the news release, you wait for price to draw to the cluster of new week/day opening gaps above price — or even into a fair value gap.

While going to premium, price will grab the short-term highs as buy-side liquidity.

If price continues spooling after the news release, you should wait for 09:30 AM (equity market open) to get an A-plus trade setup.

When price reaches premium, drawing to the pool of inefficiency, look for an [ICT Market Structure Shift](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-market-structure-shift/>) on the 1-minute timeframe — and execute a sell trade at the breaker block or fair value gap when price retraces above the 50% level.

![ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 4 — chart before the 08:30 AM news release with price sandwiched between two NDOG levels in the premium zone](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-4-before-news.png)

![ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 4 — chart after the 08:30 AM news release with price drawing to the gap cluster, MSS on the 1-min and short entry at the breaker block](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/after-news-ict-2024-mentorship.png)

In this case your stop loss will be above the high formed before the Market Structure Shift, and for take profit you target the NDOG or NWOG as the draw-on-liquidity. Alternatively you can target old lows like the previous session low, the previous day low or relative equal lows.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-4
section: (II) Bullish Bias
content:
#### (II) Bullish Bias

If your [daily bias](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-daily-bias-explained/>) is bullish on the news day, you find New Day Opening Gaps and New Week Opening Gaps below price in the [discount](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-premium-and-discount-zone-identification/>) zone. If there is no gap, you can look for a Fair Value Gap or an Inversion Fair Value Gap.

Most often, before the news at 08:30 AM, price looks sandwiched between two levels that could be a gap.

At 08:30 AM, after the news release, you wait for price to draw to the cluster of new week/day opening gaps below price — or even into a fair value gap.

While going to discount, price will grab the short-term lows as sell-side liquidity.

If price continues spooling after the news release, you should wait for 09:30 AM (equity market open) to get an A-plus trade setup.

When price reaches the discount zone, drawing to the pool of inefficiency, look for an [ICT Market Structure Shift](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-market-structure-shift/>) on the 1-minute timeframe — and execute a buy trade at the breaker block or fair value gap when price retraces below the 50% level.

![ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 4 — 4-hour chart showing the bullish news-day setup with NDOG/NWOG below price in the discount zone](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/4H-ICT-2024-Mentorship.png)

![ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 4 — 1-minute chart showing the bullish entry at the breaker block after the MSS confirms the upside delivery](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/01-minute-ICT-2024-mentorship.png)

In this case your stop loss will be below the low formed before the Market Structure Shift, and for take profit you target the NDOG or NWOG as the draw-on-liquidity. Alternatively you can target old highs like the previous session high, the previous day high or relative equal highs.

**NOTE:** If price just tests the 1st quarter (0.25 level) of the gap and runs away, this indicates that price is not going to test the consequent encroachment level of the gap and is not going to fill the gap.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-4
section: Step-by-Step Lecture 4 Trade Flow
content:
#### Step-by-Step Lecture 4 Trade Flow

This is the exact sequence Michael Huddleston walks through in Lecture 4 for news days.

  1. **Annotate the active NDOGs and the NWOG.** Use the daily chart and mark the gap clusters above and below current price.
  2. **Apply the Quarters Fibonacci on each gap.** 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.0 — the 0.25 and 0.50 levels are the most reactive references.
  3. **Set the daily bias.** Bearish targets gap clusters above (premium); bullish targets gap clusters below (discount).
  4. **Sit before 08:30 AM NY time.** Note that price often looks sandwiched between two gap levels just before the release.
  5. **Watch the 08:30 AM news release.** Do not trade the headline — let price draw toward the gap cluster.
  6. **Wait for the 09:30 AM equity-market open.** If price is still spooling after the news, the 09:30 open often delivers the A-plus setup.
  7. **Wait for the 1-minute MSS.** Confirmation of the reversal at the gap cluster.
  8. **Enter at the retracement.** Sell at the breaker block or FVG when price retraces above the 50% level (bearish); buy at the breaker block or FVG when price retraces below the 50% level (bullish).
  9. **Set the stop.** Above the high before the MSS (shorts) or below the low before the MSS (longs).
  10. **Take profit at the gap or old highs/lows.** NDOG/NWOG, prior session high/low, prior day high/low, relative equal levels.
  11. **Read the 0.25 signal.** If price taps only the 0.25 quarter and runs away, expect the gap not to fill on this leg — adjust expectations.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-4
section: Common Mistakes on the Lecture 4 Model
content:
#### Common Mistakes on the Lecture 4 Model

These are the recurring mistakes I see when traders first try to apply the Lecture 4 framework.

  1. **Trading the news headline.** The lecture explicitly tells you to ignore the numbers and read the chart. Trying to interpret CPI or NFP versus expectations leads to whipsaw entries.
  2. **Pre-positioning before 08:30 AM.** The release is the catalyst. Entries before 08:30 front-run the setup.
  3. **Skipping the 09:30 AM open.** If price is still spooling after the release, the A-plus setup is the 09:30 NYSE open — not the 08:30 reaction.
  4. **Wrong gap-to-bias pairing.** Bearish bias targets gaps above price (premium). Bullish bias targets gaps below price (discount). Reversing the pairing inverts the trade.
  5. **Ignoring the 0.25 signal.** If price taps only the 0.25 quarter and runs, the gap is not going to fill on this leg. Holding for a deeper retracement misses the move.
  6. **Stop too tight.** The stop must sit beyond the entire MSS swing — not just at the MSS pivot.

Brief answers to the questions readers ask most often about Lecture 4.

**What does ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 4 cover?**

Lecture 4 covers the news-day model anchored to the 08:30 AM US economic-news release and the 09:30 AM equity-market open. The framework uses NDOG and NWOG gap clusters as the draw-on-liquidity, with entries at the breaker block or fair value gap after a 1-minute MSS.

**What time does the Lecture 4 model start?**

You should be at the screen before 08:30 AM (news release) and ready for the 09:30 AM equity-market open. Both times are New York local.

**Why does Lecture 4 say to ignore the news numbers?**

The lecture explicitly says the charts tell the real story. The news release is the catalyst that draws price to the gap cluster — but the entry comes from the chart structure (MSS, FVG, breaker), not from the headline.

**What are the Quarters of a Gap?**

The Quarters of a Gap are the Fibonacci levels 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.0 applied to an NDOG or NWOG. The 0.25 and 0.50 levels are the most reactive references inside the gap.

**What does it mean if price tests only the 0.25 level?**

If price taps only the 0.25 quarter and runs away, this indicates that price is not going to test the consequent encroachment (50%) of the gap and is not going to fill the gap on this leg.

**What is the 09:30 AM “A-plus” setup?**

If price is still spooling after the 08:30 AM news release, the 09:30 AM equity-market open delivers the highest-conviction setup of the day. The MSS at 09:30 typically completes the move toward the gap cluster.

**How do I trade a bearish news day?**

With bearish bias, find NDOG/NWOG above price in the premium zone. After the 08:30 release wait for price to draw to the gap cluster, look for a 1-minute MSS, then sell at the breaker block or FVG when price retraces above 50%. Stop above the pre-MSS high; target NDOG/NWOG or old lows.

**How do I trade a bullish news day?**

With bullish bias, find NDOG/NWOG below price in the discount zone. After the 08:30 release wait for price to draw to the gap cluster, look for a 1-minute MSS, then buy at the breaker block or FVG when price retraces below 50%. Stop below the pre-MSS low; target NDOG/NWOG or old highs.

**What instruments work best for Lecture 4?**

NQ, ES, XAU/USD, GBP/USD and EUR/USD — instruments most reactive to US 08:30 ET news and the 09:30 NYSE open.

Yes — the free PDF download button is available on the page. The PDF is sponsored by ICTPDF.COM.

# ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 5 Notes — Asian Session NDOG Trading + Free PDF

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-2024/ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-5/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-2024/ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-5/)

![ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 5 — notes on Asian-session trading using the New Day Opening Gap \(NDOG\) for traders with 9-to-5 jobs](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ICT-2024-Mentorship-Lecture-5.png)

In the 5th lecture of the ICT 2024 mentorship program, the spotlight shifts to trading strategies tailored for the Asian session — a time often overlooked by many traders.

While ICT himself prefers to avoid trading during these less volatile hours, this session is designed specifically for those who, due to a 9-to-5 job or other commitments, cannot participate in the bustling US trading hours.

This lecture delves into how traders can effectively navigate the Asian session, with a particular focus on understanding the dynamics of the New Day Opening Gap.

For those looking to capitalise on opportunities when the traditional trading windows are closed, this session offers valuable insights and strategies to make the most of a typically quieter market.

Below are my full Lecture 5 notes — the key elements, the key timeframes, the bullish and bearish Asian-session models, the 06:00 PM gap setup, the 07:00 to 09:00 PM trading window and the free PDF download.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-5
section: Lecture 5 Quick Summary
content:
#### Lecture 5 Quick Summary

ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 5 is the Asian-session model for traders with 9-to-5 jobs. The key reference is the New Day Opening Gap (NDOG) at the 06:00 PM NY local open. The session window runs from 07:00 PM (when the algorithm becomes active and seeks liquidity) to 09:00 PM. Traders mark the NDOG high and low, mark its consequent encroachment if the gap is over 20 pips, identify the initial buy-side and sell-side liquidity (the first short-term swing high and low after the gap opens), and use the OTE pattern after 07:00 PM to enter once price has closed above (bullish) or below (bearish) the NDOG.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-5
section: Key Elements (Definitions)
content:
#### Key Elements (Definitions)

**(I) New Day Opening Gap :** abbreviated as [NDOG](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-new-day-opening-gap-ndog/>) — it is the gap between the closing price at 05:00 PM (NY local time) and the opening price at 06:00 PM (NY local time).

**(II) New Week Opening Gap :** abbreviated as [NWOG](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-new-week-opening-gap-nwog/>) — it is the gap between the closing price on Friday at 05:00 PM (NY local time) and the opening price on Monday at 06:00 PM (NY local time).

**(III)[Market Structure Shift](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-market-structure-shift/>) :** is the initial change in the delivery of price which indicates a short-term change in trend.

**(IV)[Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/fair-value-gap-trading-strategy/>) :** is a three-candle formation having a gap between the 1st and 3rd candle’s wicks.

**(V)[Inverse Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-inversion-fair-value-gap/>) :** is a failed fair value gap which works inversely.

**(VI)[Breaker Block](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-breaker-block-trading/>) :** is a failed order block.

**(VII)[Liquidity Sweep](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-liquidity-sweep-vs-liquidity-run/>) :** is the phenomenon of hunting liquidity above highs and below lows.

**(VIII) Relative Equal Highs :** is when a high has a lower swing high on the right side of it formed due to price swing failure.

**(IX) Relative Equal Lows :** is when a swing low has a higher swing low on the right side of it formed due to price swing failure.

**(X)[Consequent Encroachment](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-consequent-encroachment/>) :** is the 50% retracement level of a PD array.

**(XI) Quarters of a Gap :** use the following Fibonacci settings to find the quarter levels of a New Day Opening Gap or a New Week Opening Gap — 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.

**(XII)[Premium and Discount](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-premium-and-discount-zone-identification/>) :** the premium zone is above the 50% retracement level between an established high and low, while the discount zone is below the 50% retracement.

**(XIII)[Breakaway Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-breakaway-gap/>) :** is a fair value gap left unmitigated.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-5
section: Application in the Market
content:
#### Application in the Market

This model is specifically designed for people doing a 9-to-5 job and having no time to look for the trade during the New York session.

At 05:00 PM (NY local time) trading stops, and resumes at 06:00 PM (Asian session). This is the least enticing time of the day to trade.

Most often at 07:00 PM the algorithm becomes active and seeks liquidity. If it does not happen, leave it — because it will be a typical rangy day.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-5
section: Bullish Scenario
content:
#### Bullish Scenario

At 06:00 PM price opens with a gap called the [New Day Opening Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-new-day-opening-gap-ndog/>) — mark the high and low of the NDOG.

If the NDOG is more than 20 pips, mark its [consequent encroachment](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-consequent-encroachment/>). If the gap is less than 20 pips, you do not need to mark the consequent encroachment.

Do not trade the gap initially after the price opens. Instead, wait for price to give a clue.

Mark the short-term buy-side and sell-side liquidity (swing high and swing low).

Now wait for price to move away from the gap and grab the short-term buy-side liquidity, forming a [swing high](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-high-explained/>) which will be marked as **initial buy-side liquidity**.

Then wait for price to trade below the New Day Opening Gap and grab the short-term sell-side liquidity, forming a [swing low](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-low-formation/>) which will be termed **initial sell-side liquidity**.

Now you have initial buy-side and initial sell-side liquidity levels — and you will look for the larger pool of liquidity above and below them.

After 07:00 PM to 09:00 PM you will use these reference points to execute the trade.

After 07:00 PM, if price moves away from the NDOG and closes above it, you can look for a bullish trade setup using the [ICT Optimal Trade Entry Pattern](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-optimal-trade-entry-ote-pattern/>).

![ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 5 bullish setup — Asian-session NDOG opens at 06:00 PM, price grabs initial liquidity, closes above the NDOG and the OTE buy entry triggers between 07:00 and 09:00 PM](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-5.png)

In this scenario your stop loss will be below the low formed post-07:00 PM, and for take profit you target the initial buy-side liquidity or the larger pool of liquidity above it.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-5
section: Bearish Scenario
content:
#### Bearish Scenario

Look for the NDOG at the 06:00 PM opening price.

Do not trade the gap initially after the price opens. Wait for price to give a clue.

Mark the nearest buy-side and sell-side liquidity (swing high and swing low).

Now wait for price to move below the gap and grab the nearest sell-side liquidity, forming a [swing low](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-low-formation/>) which will be marked as **initial sell-side liquidity**.

Then wait for price to trade away from the New Day Opening Gap and grab the nearest buy-side liquidity, forming a [swing high](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-swing-high-explained/>) which will be termed **initial buy-side liquidity**.

Now you have initial buy-side and initial sell-side liquidity levels — and you will look for the larger pool of liquidity above and below the initial liquidity levels.

After 07:00 PM to 09:00 PM you will use these reference points to execute the trade.

After 07:00 PM, if price goes below the NDOG and closes below it, you can look for a bearish trade setup using the [ICT Optimal Trade Entry Pattern](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-optimal-trade-entry-ote-pattern/>).

In this scenario your stop loss will be above the high formed post-07:00 PM, and for take profit you target the initial sell-side liquidity or the larger pool of liquidity below it.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-5
section: Step-by-Step Lecture 5 Trade Flow
content:
#### Step-by-Step Lecture 5 Trade Flow

This is the exact sequence Michael Huddleston walks through in Lecture 5 for the Asian-session model.

  1. **Sit down before 06:00 PM NY time.** The session window starts when the New Day Opening Gap forms.
  2. **Mark the NDOG.** High and low of the gap between the 05:00 PM close and the 06:00 PM open.
  3. **Mark the consequent encroachment if NDOG over 20 pips.** The 50% midpoint of the gap.
  4. **Wait — do not trade the open.** Let price give a clue before committing.
  5. **Mark the initial buy-side liquidity.** The first short-term swing high formed away from the gap.
  6. **Mark the initial sell-side liquidity.** The first short-term swing low formed away from the gap.
  7. **Wait for the algorithm at 07:00 PM.** If price does not start seeking liquidity by 07:00 PM, sit out — it is a rangy day.
  8. **Watch for the directional close at 07:00 PM.** A close above the NDOG signals bullish; a close below signals bearish.
  9. **Apply OTE for the entry.** Use the [ICT Optimal Trade Entry](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-optimal-trade-entry-ote-pattern/>) 0.62 to 0.79 retracement on the leg that just developed.
  10. **Set the stop.** Below the post-07:00 PM low (longs) or above the post-07:00 PM high (shorts).
  11. **Take profit at the initial liquidity.** Initial buy-side (longs) or initial sell-side (shorts) — extend to the larger pool if the trade has room.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-5
section: Best Markets for the Lecture 5 Asian-Session Model
content:
#### Best Markets for the Lecture 5 Asian-Session Model

The model is anchored to the 06:00 PM NY-local Asian-session reopen, so it works best on instruments active during this window.

  * **USD/JPY, AUD/JPY and AUD/USD** — the most active forex pairs during the Asian session, where NDOGs deliver the cleanest signatures.
  * **NQ (NASDAQ futures)** and **ES (S &P 500 futures)** — the CME Globex 06:00 PM ET reopen produces a visible NDOG on US indices.
  * **XAU/USD (Gold)** — gold’s Asian-session NDOG often delivers an OTE trade between 07:00 and 09:00 PM ET.

**For traders in the United States** who follow the CFTC FIFO and no-hedge rules and who work a 9-to-5 day job, the Lecture 5 Asian-session model is the natural fit. NQ and ES on CME Globex reopen at 06:00 PM ET and deliver the OTE setup between 07:00 and 09:00 PM ET — a window that is fully outside US daytime working hours and aligns with most evening schedules.

title: ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-5
section: Common Mistakes on the Lecture 5 Model
content:
#### Common Mistakes on the Lecture 5 Model

These are the recurring mistakes I see when traders first try to apply the Lecture 5 framework.

  1. **Trading the 06:00 PM gap immediately.** The lecture explicitly says do not trade the gap right after the open. Wait for price to give a clue.
  2. **Skipping the 20-pip CE rule.** If the NDOG is over 20 pips, the consequent encroachment must be marked. Skipping it removes the most reactive level inside the gap.
  3. **Forcing trades on a rangy day.** If the algorithm is not active by 07:00 PM, the framework explicitly says sit out. Trying to force a trade in a rangy Asian session produces chop entries.
  4. **Skipping the directional close.** The bullish setup requires a close above the NDOG; the bearish setup requires a close below. Entering before that close inverts the read.
  5. **Wrong instrument for the session.** Asian-session trading is most effective on JPY pairs and US index futures. Trying to trade GBP or EUR pairs during the Asian session usually produces no setup.
  6. **Stop too tight.** Stops must sit beyond the entire post-07:00 PM swing — not just at the OTE entry level.

This approach helps us identify the precise moments when market shifts occur, allowing us to harness the power of time in our trading strategies. In this course, you will learn a real, tradeable model based on the timing of price actions, providing a more refined and actionable perspective on market dynamics.

title: lecture-1
section: Lecture 1 Quick Summary
content:
#### Lecture 1 Quick Summary

The ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 1 introduces the time-based mentorship model. The session begins with the trader at the screen by 08:00 AM New York local time and focuses on price delivery after 08:30 AM. Three timeframes are used: 15-minute (bias and draw-on-liquidity), 5-minute (structure context) and 1-minute (entry trigger). The bias is built around relative equal highs/lows, the entry comes from a Market Structure Shift after the liquidity raid, and the trade is taken from a PD array — order block, breaker or fair value gap (BISI/SIBI) — left behind by the displacement.

title: lecture-1
section: Key Elements (Definitions)
content:
#### Key Elements (Definitions)

**(I) Relative Equal High :** is a high having a lower swing high on the right side of it, formed because of a swing failure and a potential reversal.

**(II) Relative Equal Low :** is a low having a higher swing low on the right side of it, formed because of a swing failure and a potential reversal.

**(III) Displacement :** is a move against a pre-session, pre-day or pre-price swing — so it is a counter move.

**(IV)[ICT Order Block](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-order-block/>) :** is the zone or area in a price chart where a large number of orders are executed by institutional traders in the market and price shows a sudden, strong move from that area.

**(V) Breaker Block :** is when price sweeps the liquidity of a low or relative equal lows by dropping below the low and then it goes up breaking the previous swing high. All the up-closed candles formed before dropping down and sweeping the liquidity are the bullish breaker block, but the most sensitive one is the last up-closed candlestick.

![Bullish breaker block — sweep of the relative equal low followed by a reclaim of the prior swing high; the last up-closed candle before the drop is the most sensitive zone](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/bullish-breaker.png)

A bearish breaker block is when price sweeps the liquidity of a high or relative equal highs by going above them and then it drops down breaking the previous swing low. All the down-closed candles formed before moving up and sweeping the liquidity are the bearish breaker block, but the most sensitive one is the last down-closed candlestick.

![Bearish breaker block — sweep of the relative equal high followed by a break of the prior swing low; the last down-closed candle before the rise is the most sensitive zone](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/bearish-breaker.png)

**(VI) SIBI :** is a down-closed [ICT Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/fair-value-gap-trading-strategy/>).

**(VII) BISI :** is an up-closed [ICT Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/fair-value-gap-trading-strategy/>).

**(VIII) NWOG :** [New Week Opening Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-new-week-opening-gap-nwog/>) is the gap between Friday’s closing price and Sunday’s opening price.

section: Key Time of the Day

title: lecture-1
section: Application in the Market
content:
#### Application in the Market

According to ICT 2024 mentorship lecture 1, you have to sit at your computer before 08:30 AM (New York local time), preferably at 08:00 AM (New York local time).

You only have to focus on three timeframes — 15 Minutes, 5 Minutes and 1 Minute.

The 15-minute chart is your bias and parent chart, where you look for levels like inefficiencies and draw on liquidity.

After 08:00 AM you look for relative equal highs or relative equal lows on the 1-minute timeframe.

After the formation of relative equal highs/lows, wait for price to grab those relative equal highs/lows.

title: lecture-1
section: (I) Bearish Scenario
content:
#### (I) Bearish Scenario

If price forms and grabs the relative equal highs then wait for price to return back to range and close below the swing low (Market Structure Shift).

After grabbing the liquidity of relative equal highs, if price returns back and closes below the swing low, mark the bearish order block, the SIBI formed in the dropping move and the bearish breaker block formed after breaking the swing low.

When price retraces to the order block, the SIBI or the breaker you can execute a sell trade at one of these PD-arrays — targeting the next draw on liquidity like relative equal lows or the low of the previous session.

![ICT 2024 mentorship Lecture 1 bearish setup — sweep of the relative equal highs, MSS to the downside and short entry from the SIBI or bearish breaker](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ICT-mentorship-2024-lecture-1-sell.png)

Your stop loss will be above the high formed post 08:30 AM.

title: lecture-1
section: (II) Bullish Scenario
content:
#### (II) Bullish Scenario

If price forms and grabs the relative equal lows then wait for price to return back to range and close above the swing high (Market Structure Shift).

After grabbing the liquidity of relative equal lows, if price returns back and closes above the swing high, mark the bullish order block, the BISI formed in the rising move and the bullish breaker block formed after breaking the swing high.

When price retraces to the order block, the BISI or the bullish breaker you can execute a buy trade at one of these PD-arrays — targeting the next draw on liquidity like relative equal highs or the high of the previous session.

![ICT 2024 mentorship Lecture 1 bullish setup — sweep of the relative equal lows, MSS to the upside and long entry from the BISI or bullish breaker](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/BULLISH-ICT-MENTORSHIP-2024.png)

Your stop loss will be below the low formed post 08:30 AM.

  8. **Set the stop.** Above the high formed post-08:30 AM (shorts) or below the low formed post-08:30 AM (longs).
  9. **Take profit at the next draw.** Relative equal lows / previous session low (bearish) or relative equal highs / previous session high (bullish).

# ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 2 Notes — 07:00 AM Liquidity Hunt + IFVG Entry & Free PDF

**Source:** [https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-2024/mentorship-lecture-2/](https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-2024/mentorship-lecture-2/)

![ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 2 — notes on the 07:00 AM liquidity hunt, inverse fair value gap \(IFVG\) and breaker block entry with Fibonacci targets](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ICT-2024-Mentorship-Lecture-2.png)

In the second lecture notes of the ICT 2024 Mentorship program, we explore the details of post-7:00 AM price delivery — with a particular focus on the liquidity hunt of relative equal highs and lows.

This session emphasises the importance of recognising and using the inverse fair value gap (IFVG) and the breaker block, all through the strategic application of the Fibonacci tool.

By understanding these core concepts, traders can better anticipate market moves and refine their trading strategies in the dynamic morning market conditions.

Below are my full Lecture 2 notes — the key elements, the key times, the bullish and bearish scenarios, the Fibonacci targets and the free PDF download.

title: mentorship-lecture-2
section: Lecture 2 Quick Summary
content:
#### Lecture 2 Quick Summary

ICT 2024 Mentorship Lecture 2 builds on the time-based model from Lecture 1 by shifting the entry from the 08:30 NY-AM model to the post-07:00 AM AM-session retrace. The session opens with the trader at the screen by 07:00 AM New York local time. The first move retraces back into the London-session range, then sweeps relative equal highs or lows. The trade is taken from the consequent encroachment of the IFVG (inverse fair value gap) — or from the breaker block if the IFVG is not present. Stops sit beyond the post-07:00 AM liquidity-hunt swing, and the Fibonacci is drawn from that swing back to the 07:00 AM opening price for -2 and -2.5 extension targets.

title: mentorship-lecture-2
section: Key Elements (Definitions)
content:
#### Key Elements (Definitions)

**(I) SIBI :** is the down-closed [Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/fair-value-gap-trading-strategy/>).

**(II) BISI :** is the up-closed [Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/fair-value-gap-trading-strategy/>).

**(III) IFVG :** is the [Inversion Fair Value Gap](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-inversion-fair-value-gap/>).

**(IV)[Breaker Block](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-breaker-block-trading/>) :** is a failed order block.

**(V) Relative Equal High :** is when a high has a lower swing high on the right side of it, formed due to price swing failure.

**(VI) Relative Equal Low :** is when a swing low has a higher swing low on the right side of it, formed due to price swing failure.

**(VII) Fractal :** is the repetitive nature of price behaviour on every timeframe.

**(VIII) Specific :** the very first fair value gap prior to the stop hunt will be the most sensitive inverse fair value gap.

**(IX)[Consequent Encroachment](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-consequent-encroachment/>):** is the 50% retracement level (middle) of an ICT [PD Array](<https://innercircletrader.net/tutorials/ict-pd-array-key-to-trade-execution/>).

**(X) Fibonacci Inputs :** use 0, 0.5, 1, -2 and -2.5.

section: Application in the Market
content:
#### Application in the Market

Start at 07:00 AM (New York local time). Do not look at anything prior if you are brand new. If you have experience you can look at prior data (London price delivery).

Anything you want to see prior to 07:00 AM is the London high and low for the draw on liquidity.

Do not predict the price — just wait for it to happen.

The 07:00 AM (AM-session) first and foremost characteristic is retracing back into the London-session range.

At 07:00 AM you should be at your computer and you have to look for relative equal highs or relative equal lows forming on the 5-minute or 1-minute timeframe.

After the formation of relative equal highs or lows, wait for price to grab those relative equal levels.

title: mentorship-lecture-2
section: (I) Bearish Scenario
content:
#### (I) Bearish Scenario

If price forms and grabs the relative equal highs, then wait for price to return back to range and close below the swing low (Market Structure Shift).

After grabbing the liquidity of relative equal highs, if price returns back and closes below the swing low, mark the very first fair value gap formed prior to the stop hunt as the IFVG and also mark the bearish breaker block formed after the break of the swing low.

When price retraces back, execute a sell trade at the consequent encroachment of the Inverse Fair Value Gap (IFVG) marked. If the IFVG is not present, you can execute the sell trade at the bearish breaker block.

![ICT 2024 mentorship Lecture 2 bearish setup — 07:00 AM sweep of relative equal highs, MSS to the downside and short entry from the IFVG consequent encroachment](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ICT-mentorship-2024-lecture-2-sell.png)

Your stop loss in this scenario will be above the swing high formed post-07:00 AM liquidity hunt.

For take profit you can target the next draw on liquidity, or you can use the Fibonacci tool by drawing it from the high formed post-07:00 AM liquidity hunt to the lowest low at 07:00 AM (the opening price of 07:00 AM).

You can set your take profit at the -2 or -2.5 Fibonacci retracement levels.

title: mentorship-lecture-2
section: (II) Bullish Scenario
content:
#### (II) Bullish Scenario

If price forms and grabs the relative equal lows, then wait for price to return back to range and close above the swing high (Market Structure Shift).

After grabbing the liquidity of relative equal lows, if price returns back and closes above the swing high, mark the very first fair value gap formed prior to the stop hunt as the IFVG and also mark the bullish breaker block formed after the break of the swing high.

When price retraces back, execute a buy trade at the consequent encroachment of the Inverse Fair Value Gap (IFVG) marked. If the IFVG is not present, you can execute the buy trade at the bullish breaker block.

![ICT 2024 mentorship Lecture 2 bullish setup — 07:00 AM sweep of relative equal lows, MSS to the upside and long entry from the IFVG consequent encroachment](https://innercircletrader.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/ict-2024-mentorship-lecture-2-buy.png)

Your stop loss in this scenario will be below the swing low formed post-07:00 AM liquidity hunt.

For take profit you can target the next draw on liquidity, or you can use the Fibonacci tool by drawing it from the low formed post-07:00 AM liquidity hunt to the highest high at 07:00 AM (the opening price of 07:00 AM).

You can set your take profit at the -2 or -2.5 Fibonacci retracement levels.

**NOTE:** After 07:00 AM, 08:00 AM and 09:00 AM in the first 30 minutes (pre-session range), expect something opposite — opposite price movement to the relative trend or relative equal highs/lows.

title: mentorship-lecture-2
section: Step-by-Step Lecture 2 Trade Flow
content:
#### Step-by-Step Lecture 2 Trade Flow

This is the exact sequence Michael Huddleston walks through in Lecture 2, condensed into a checklist you can run before every NY AM session.

  1. **Sit down before 07:00 AM NY time.** The setup is built between 07:00 and the first 30 minutes of the AM session.
  2. **Mark the London high and low.** These are the only references you need from the prior session — they become the draw-on-liquidity for the AM open.
  3. **Do not predict.** Wait for price to actually print relative equal highs or relative equal lows on the 5-minute or 1-minute chart.
  4. **Wait for the liquidity hunt.** Price must take out the relative equal level after 07:00 AM.
  5. **Wait for the MSS.** A clean close below the prior swing low (bearish) or above the prior swing high (bullish) confirms the shift.
  6. **Mark the IFVG.** The very first fair value gap prior to the stop hunt becomes the most sensitive Inverse Fair Value Gap.
  7. **Mark the breaker block.** The breaker block forms after the break of the swing low (bearish) or swing high (bullish) — it is the backup entry zone if no IFVG is present.
  8. **Enter at the CE of the IFVG.** Wait for price to retrace into the consequent encroachment (50% midpoint) of the IFVG and execute. If no IFVG, enter at the breaker block.
  9. **Set the stop.** Above the post-07:00 AM swing high (shorts) or below the post-07:00 AM swing low (longs).
  10. **Take profit at -2 / -2.5.** Draw the Fibonacci from the post-07:00 AM swing back to the 07:00 AM opening price and stage exits at the -2 and -2.5 extensions, or use the next draw on liquidity.
